# HMA LIA 1500-2000 Project Facts



Last updated: 2026-08-22 (Round 223: keep current production climate; retain NETP MJJ only as a regional temporal research product)


This is the canonical project contract. Read it before every LIA simulation,

diagnosis, plot, or parameter search. It separates verified facts from pending

decisions so that old experiments are not mistaken for the current design.



## 1. Scientific objective



- Reconstruct the missing 1500-2000 ice-volume evolution of 191 HMA LIA glacier

  systems.

- LIA and modern/RGI geometries are endpoint constraints. The simulated curve

  fills the unobserved interval.

- Final validation asks whether the 1901-2000 part agrees with independent

  observations and whether glacier-wise parameter maps are spatially coherent.

- The current state-search experiment uses **length as the observational

  scoring variable** and volume only for spin-up stability. Area and volume are

  always saved but do not enter the observational endpoint score.



## 2. Glacier identity



- The population is 191 **LIA systems**, identified by `lia_unique_id`.

- RGI IDs identify modern members or the mapped main RGI glacier. They must not

  replace the LIA-system identity when selecting experiments.

- Current three-system pilot: small `1545`, medium `1044`, large `3584`.

- Systems `3144`, `2907`, and `2692` are excluded from this three-system pilot

  by explicit user decision. This is not a claim that they are abnormal.



## 3. Climate contract



- Monthly climatology: GSWP3-W5E5, 1961-1990.

- Temperature forcing: W5E5 monthly climatology plus reconstructed annual

  temperature anomaly.

- `temp_std`: W5E5 and fixed in time.

- Precipitation-anomaly on/off is an explicit experiment switch. Do not enable

  precipitation anomalies unless the active experiment requests it.

- `prcp_fac` and precipitation anomalies are different controls and must not be

  described as the same thing.

- CRU CL is not the climatological baseline for the current workflow.



## 4. Length definitions: mandatory geometry contract



There are two distinct objects:



1. **Spatial main-flowline length**: length along the mapped LIA or RGI glacier

   centerline in projected coordinates.

2. **OGGM elevation-band model length**: number of ice-covered nodes along a

   synthetic one-dimensional pseudo-flowline multiplied by node spacing.



They are comparable only if the elevation-band construction was explicitly

scaled to the spatial main-flowline target and the mapping was verified.



Main-line selection rules:



- LIA network: use the stored `main_branch_index`.

- Modern OGGM centerlines: use the unique root with `flows_to is None`.

- Never select a main line merely by list position, RGI ID, or visual guess.



Verified example, LIA system 3584:



| Quantity | Verified length |

|---|---:|

| Registered LIA target | 24.130 km |

| Spatial LIA main branch 18 | 24.147 km |

| OGGM inversion-flowline 1-D axis | 21.470 km |

| OGGM modern root centerline index 3 | 22.357 km |

| Existing first-10 elevation-band initial ice | 9.900 km |



Conclusion for 3584: the spatial main line was selected correctly. The old

9.900 km value came from an elevation-band build whose target equaled its

unscaled hypsometric pseudo-length, not the mapped LIA main-line target. The

corrected elevation-band initial length is 24.150 km for a 24.1468 km spatial

target.



The earlier `21.470 km` label is corrected here. It is not an independent GIS

or registered spatial target. `modern_tau_calibration.py` computes it as the

modern inversion-flowline axis length, `(114 - 1) x 190 m`. The `22.357 km`

value is the projected spatial arc length of the unique root in

`centerlines.pkl`. The current `selected_five_length_targets.csv` therefore

retains `22.357119 km` for the spatial-length endpoint contract. Replacing it

with `21.470 km` would mix the Core-191 LIA spatially scaled pseudo-axis with a

separately resampled modern model axis unless a new ratio-based model-scale

contract were explicitly approved.

Therefore:



- Do not compare the old 9.900 km model length directly with the 24.130 km LIA

  target.

- Do not use physical parameters to compensate for this geometry mismatch.

- A length-scored batch may start only after each input model length uses the

  same declared length definition as its target and differs by no more than the

  accepted 10% tolerance.



## 5. Historical D-layer LHS experiment



This section records the completed original D-layer LHS design. It is not the

current B-window adaptive state-search configuration and must not be used as a

template for new runs.



- Spin-up climate window: 1807-1836.

- Transient start year: 1836.

- Spin-up duration: fixed 500 years.

- Save spin-up geometry snapshots every 100 years.

- Run from 1836 to 2000 after spin-up.

- LHS size: 200 points per glacier, three glaciers, 600 chains total.

- Parallel target: up to 12 processes after the single-chain preflight passes.



Parameter space:



| Parameter | Range | Sampling |

|---|---:|---|

| `delta_t` | -3 to +1.5 K | uniform |

| `melt_f` | 2.5 to 7.5 kg m-2 d-1 K-1 | uniform |

| `prcp_fac` | Stage-2 initial value x 0.8 to 1.2 | uniform |

| `glen_a` | OGGM default x 0.5 to 3 | log-uniform |

| `temp_melt` | -2 to 0 degC | uniform |



Not sampled: `fs` and the rain/snow threshold.



Scores:



- `E_LIA = abs(L_spinup - L_LIA) / L_LIA`

- `E_2000 = abs(L_2000 - L_RGI) / L_RGI`

- `E_total = E_LIA + E_2000`

- Crashes are rejected.

- Length below 5% or above 200% of initial model length is recorded as

  `out_of_range`.

- Volume, area, snapshots, and runtime are recorded but not scored.



## 6. Required preflight before any batch



For every selected LIA system, print and save:



- `lia_unique_id` and mapped main `rgi_id`;

- LIA main-branch index and spatial length;

- RGI root-flowline index and spatial length;

- elevation-band target length, initial ice length, and node spacing;

- the exact length definition used by `E_LIA` and `E_2000`;

- relative mismatch between model and target length definitions.



Hard stop conditions:



- wrong or ambiguous main branch/root;

- target source missing;

- model and target use different length definitions;

- initial length mismatch greater than 10%;

- requested precipitation-anomaly mode is unclear;

- a single complete chain has not passed before launching the batch.

- The accepted trajectories are dynamically selective: 1044 has a median

  while 3584 has a median length range of 0.300 km and median volume net

- A controlled annual-response test was completed for accepted system 3584,

  point 179. Both branches start from the same saved spin-up geometry and use

  reconstructed temperature forcing; the control repeats the 1807-1836

  climate. The 1.033 K reconstructed temperature-anomaly range produces an

  annual climatic-MB standard deviation of 154.5 kg m-2 yr-1 and correlations

  of -0.994 with both climatic MB and volume-derived dynamic MB. Therefore the

- A signed finite-difference Jacobian was built from those 33 OFAT chains and

  used to propose a bounded ridge/trust-region update. The response matrices

  objective improvement was only 4.6% for 1044 and 1.8% for 3584, while 1545

  worsened from 99.74 to 595.02. Therefore this local Jacobian route must not

  drive further automatic parameter proposals. Diagnostics and verification

  were `1044/+1.0 K` (19.78%, 0.21%), `1545/+1.0 K` (18.62%, 0.47%), and

  `3584/+1.5 K` (46.16%, 13.65%), where each pair is LIA-length error and

  300-500-year volume change. Results are in

  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/layered_coordinate_search_v1/layer1_delta_t_profile_v3/`.

- Layer 2 profiled directed Stage-2 `melt_f` multipliers while re-profiling

  `delta_t` at every multiplier: 75 design points, 66 new real OGGM chains and

  9 strictly validated Layer-1 reuses. All 75 were numerically clean. System

  `1044` has two accepted points; the best is `melt_f x0.8` and

  `delta_t=+1.25 K`, with 0.43% LIA-length error and 1.05% 300-500-year volume

  change. System `1545` has no accepted point: its response jumps from a long,

  strongly evolving branch to a stable branch about 18% shorter than the LIA

  target. System `3584` has no point that passes the fixed-500-year gates:

  increasing `melt_f` reduces the late spin-up volume change but collapses the

  length. This fixed-500 result does not supersede the verified 1000-year

  convergence of the Stage-2 `melt_f`, `delta_t=+0.75 K` state above; physical

  parameters must not be changed merely to force convergence by year 500.

  Results and response plots are in

  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/layered_coordinate_search_v1/layer2_melt_profile_v1/`.

- A targeted nine-chain `delta_t` bisection then resolved the sharp Layer-2

  transition had LIA-length errors of 9.14%, 7.64%, and 9.64%, but their

  300-500-year volume changes were 7.20%, 9.41%, and 6.26%. Once the volume

  change fell below 2%, the corresponding length was already 16-17% short.

  `asia_indi007B:trsgi_breit`: Thijwas A, 34.65 N, 75.47 E, 3200 m,

  *Abies pindrow*, re-standardized tree-ring index, 1805-1981.

- Every numerical mapping passed with correlation 1.0; the maximum residual

  after the standardization-equivalent affine transform was

  `8.88e-15`, and all source hashes were unchanged. The two available

  `combined_proxydata6.mat` copies have different whole-file hashes, but both

  independently produce the same record-203 and record-241 column identities

  and exact sequence closure.

- The local Mann_2008 source does not encode a seasonality field for record

  203, so do not silently assign the shorter LMR/Breitenmoser Gulmarg record's

  JJA metadata to it. Record 241 does carry LMR seasonality `[6, 7, 8]`

  (JJA), while the archived EnKF configuration uses January-December climate

  means and calibration years 1940-2000. This is a concrete PSM-seasonality

  mismatch and the next controlled climate-reconstruction experiment should

  test record 241 with JJA temperature/precipitation predictors while keeping

  the proxy chronology, all other records, prior, localization, and error

  model fixed. It is not evidence that record 241 is invalid.





- The bounded Layer-1 delta-T boundary-extension design contains 107 LIA

  systems and two new one-sided delta-T values per system (214 tasks). The

  candidate step sequence is `0.125/0.25/0.375/0.5/0.625/0.75 K`; values

  already sampled or outside `[-4.0,+2.5] K` are skipped, then the first two

  new values are retained. Its execution driver is

  `lia_191_tradeoff_pilot.py`, not the base `lia_191_controller.py` search-

  block interface.

- The mandatory preflight for system `2266` at `delta_t=+0.875 K` completed

  cleanly in 53.9 s. It used B-window 1441-1470 climate, precipitation

  anomalies off, Stage-2 `melt_f/prcp_fac/glen_a`, and `temp_melt=-1 degC`.

  Adaptive spin-up converged at year 500 with 0.562% preceding-200-year volume

  change; no technical, finite-value, CFL, or boundary failure occurred. The

  forward peak is 11.400 km versus the 12.424 km LIA target (8.24% total-

  length error), and year 2000 is 10.750 km versus the 10.678 km RGI target

  (0.67% error). It therefore passes the active provisional 10% total-length

  endpoint screen. Its 37.2% peak-to-2000 amplitude ratio remains an auxiliary

  diagnostic, not a hard rejection gate. The generic pilot `scores.csv`

  reports `accepted=false/pending-tolerance` because that legacy field uses

  the separation-routing scorer; it must not be interpreted as failure under

  the active total-length screen. The restored manifest contains one completed

  task and 213 planned tasks; the remaining tasks have not been released.



## 8. Working rules



- The active parameter-estimation loop is specified in

  `parameter_estimation_loop_v2.md`. Numerical cleanliness, adaptive spin-up

  convergence, no more than 2% preceding-200-year spin-up volume change, and

  declared geometry consistency remain hard gates. A provisional historical

  curve now requires one stable chain whose forward peak is within 10% of the

  LIA total length target and whose year-2000 endpoint is within 10% of the

  RGI total length target. The 20% LIA-RGI separation scale remains a routing

  tolerance for deciding the next parameter block; it is not the final

  observational acceptance model. The V3 corridor, minimum-at-2000, amplitude,

  and modern MB remain auxiliary diagnostics.



- Do not run curves merely to see what happens. Every run must answer a stated

  experiment question and pass its preflight.

- New layered parameter searches must use adaptive spin-up stability rather

  than treating year 500 as an equilibrium target. A fixed-500 chain may be

  reused only when it already passes the declared 200-year volume-stability

  gate. Do not tune a physical parameter merely to force earlier convergence.

- Do not introduce a parameter, precipitation switch, glacier, window, or

  scoring rule that the active plan did not request.

- Do not call a glacier normal or abnormal. Report only its response under a

  named configuration.

- Do not silently repair or skip failed glaciers.

- Do not tune physical parameters to hide an ID, geometry, unit, boundary, or

  length-definition error.

- When a verified fact changes, update this document in the same change as the

  code/configuration that changed it.

## 10. Proxy-241 seasonality experiment (2026-08-12)

- The first R2024b annual replay attempt for proxy9 record `#241` was stopped before EnKF because `load_S.m` replaces nonpositive bias-corrected precipitation values with stochastic `gamrnd(1,0.05,...)` draws. The deterministic annual chronology, coefficients, temperature predictor, and residuals matched the archived operator, while fresh precipitation differed by `0.05058896` and fresh annual `HXb` differed by `0.01461301`. This was resolved as an environment-dependent stochastic replay issue, not a proxy identity or season-definition conflict.
- A new independent common-random-number experiment then reset MATLAB R2024b to the same fixed RNG state before fresh Jan-Dec, JJA, and repeated Jan-Dec PSM calls. The repeated Jan-Dec calls matched exactly; the JJA operator was defined as archived annual `HXb` plus the fresh JJA-minus-annual `HXb` difference. Source hashes remained unchanged, and the fixed-network EnKF closure was `1.51e-14 degC`.
- For target 3584, the 1901-1950 target trend changed from `+0.0558` to `-0.0780 degC per century` (delta `-0.1338`), while the 15-year phase projection against comparison-only `rec_ref` changed from `-0.2015` to `-0.3175`. The JJA replacement therefore changes the early-20th-century signal substantially but does not resolve the phase conflict in this controlled test.
- The result is an operator-sensitivity diagnosis only. It does not validate `rec_ref`, invalidate proxy `#241`, or authorize retuning the prior, localization, error model, or other proxy operators. Outputs are in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_proxy241_jja_psm_v2_delta_anchor/`.
## 11. Proxy-271 provenance and operator audit (2026-08-12)

- Proxy9 record `#271` maps uniquely to `combined_proxydata6.mat` column `287` and public LMR record `asia_indi010B:trsgi_breit`: Kanasar, 30.75 N, 77.80 E, 2200 m, re-standardized tree-ring index, 1788-1988. The proxy9 sequence closes against both the combined column and LMR public series with correlation effectively 1.0 and maximum affine residual `8.88e-16`; all source hashes are unchanged.
- The LMR metadata declares climate variable `temperature`, relation `positive`, and seasonality JJA `[6, 7, 8]`. The archived Jan-Dec bivariate PSM instead has coefficients `[-0.0417944, -0.7758172, +0.0089143]`, calibration temperature correlation `-0.285263`, precipitation correlation `+0.096484`, and overall PSM correlation `0.285352` (`p=0.04687`). This is a documented metadata/operator-direction mismatch, not a source identity, chronology, or standardization failure.
- In the existing controlled fixed-prior EnKF attribution, record `#271` contributes a 1901-1950 target-3584 trend of `-0.8640 degC per century`. The prior holdout experiment showed that removing `#271` changes the target phase projection against comparison-only `rec_ref` from `-0.2015` to `-0.0706`, but holdout improvement does not authorize deletion or prove the record invalid.
- The next controlled experiment, if approved, must separate two questions: first replay `#271` with an unconstrained JJA bivariate PSM; only if that remains negative should a separately labeled positive-response constrained JJA branch be tested. Chronology, all other proxy operators, prior, localization, RegEM error matrix, and target extraction remain frozen. No OGGM is authorized. Outputs are in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_proxy271_audit_v1/`.

## 12. Proxy-271 unconstrained JJA PSM experiment (2026-08-12)

- A controlled no-OGGM experiment replaced only proxy9 record `#271`'s archived annual `HXb` with the common-random-number, delta-anchored JJA-minus-annual perturbation. Proxy observations, the remaining 296 proxy operators, prior, localization, RegEM-completed error matrix, target extraction, and comparison-only `rec_ref` were frozen. Source hashes remained unchanged; archived annual baseline closure was exact and maximum EnKF closure was `1.51e-14 degC`.
- The unconstrained JJA bivariate fit did **not** recover the LMR metadata's positive temperature relation. Its coefficients are `[-0.0392055, -0.1490923, -0.0759759]`: the temperature coefficient remains negative, though smaller in magnitude than the archived annual `-0.7758172`. Its overall correlation is `0.145652` with `p=0.317998`, versus the archived annual correlation `0.285352` with `p=0.046874`; JJA therefore weakens statistical support and does not resolve the documented operator-direction mismatch.
- The isolated JJA operator nevertheless changes target-3584 1901-1950 behavior: target trend changes from `+0.0558` to `+0.1426 degC per century`, and the 15-year phase projection against comparison-only `rec_ref` improves from `-0.2015` to `-0.0818`. Record `#271`'s target-trend contribution changes from `-0.8640` to `-0.1434 degC per century`. This is a sensitivity result, not validation of the JJA operator.
- Per the declared staged experiment boundary, do not automatically run a positive-response constrained branch. The unconstrained JJA fit remains negative and is statistically weaker; any constrained-sign test requires a new explicit decision and must be reported as a separate hypothesis, not a correction. Outputs are in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_proxy271_jja_psm_v1_delta_anchor/`.
## 13. Proxy-271 positive-response constrained JJA hypothesis (2026-08-12)

- An explicit second-stage hypothesis test imposed `b_temperature >= 0` on the JJA bivariate PSM for record `#271`, with intercept and precipitation coefficient free. The annual baseline, all other proxy operators, prior, localization, frozen RegEM error matrix, target extraction, and comparison-only `rec_ref` remained fixed. Source hashes were unchanged; annual anchor closure was exact and maximum EnKF closure was `1.51e-14 degC`.
- The constrained least-squares solution lies exactly at the lower boundary: coefficients `[-0.0341888, 0, -0.0632659]`. This is not evidence for a positive temperature response; the data prefer a nonpositive coefficient under the stated constraint. The constrained fit has correlation `0.133978` and `p=0.358733`, weaker than the unconstrained JJA fit (`r=0.145652`, `p=0.317998`) and much weaker than the archived annual fit (`r=0.285352`, `p=0.046874`).
- The constrained operator changes target 3584 in 1901-1950 from the baseline trend `+0.0558` to `+0.1532 degC per century`; the 15-year phase projection against comparison-only `rec_ref` changes from `-0.2015` to `-0.0666`. Record `#271`'s target-trend contribution changes from `-0.8640` to `-0.0891 degC per century`. This improves the selected phase metric but is a hypothesis sensitivity, not validation or authorization to adopt the operator.
- The positive-response constrained branch is therefore closed as a diagnostic. Do not promote it to the production reconstruction solely because it improves the phase metric; it is a boundary-constrained, statistically weak fit. Outputs are in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_proxy271_jja_positive_constraint_v1/`.

- Six chains tested systems 214, 3897, and 2005 with A-window 1171-1200
  adaptive spin-up and 1200-2000 forward forcing. Stage-2 physics, geometry,
  precipitation anomalies off, and constant delta-T were frozen.
- Anchor pairs were 214: -0.25/-0.5 K; 3897: +1.0/+0.875 K; and 2005:
  +0.375/+0.25 K. The colder anchors directly test the adjacent B-window
  stability/branch boundary; this was not a new parameter search.
- The mandatory 3897/+1.0 K preflight converged at year 700 with 0.770%
  preceding-200-year volume change. All six chains completed without technical,
  finite-value, CFL, or boundary failure.
- No branch classification changed between A and B. Stable RGI anchors retained
  year-2000 lengths of 7150 m (214), 11250 m (3897), and 22350 m (2005).
  The 214/-0.5 K and 2005/+0.25 K chains remained nonconverged/out-of-range;
  the 3897/+0.875 K stable long branch persisted at 21000 m versus 21100 m in B.
- Conclusion: switching from B to A alone did not create the missing
  intermediate stable branch and must not be expanded automatically to all 191
  systems.

  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/lia_191_a_window_branch_mechanism_v1/`.

## 16. System 3897 B-window saved-branch geometry diagnosis and observation-domain gate (2026-08-13)

- This was a read-only comparison of two completed, stable B-window chains;
  no OGGM model was advanced. The long branch uses `delta_t=+0.875 K` and the
  short/RGI branch uses `delta_t=+1.0 K`. All other Stage-2 physical parameters,
  the 1441-1470 spin-up climate, and the 1470-2000 forward forcing are identical.
- The Core input is a `RectangularBedFlowline`; OGGM `SemiImplicitModel`
  explicitly converts it to a `TrapezoidalBedFlowline` with `lambda=0`.
  The saved states retain the same bed and fixed widths node by node and satisfy
  `section = width * thickness`. The object-type change is the model's
  section-equivalent internal representation, not evidence of a changed bed,
  width, or selected main flowline.
- The 200 km downstream extension came from a historical explicit
  `--downstream-buffer 200000` build command. It was introduced after system
  1545 produced `RuntimeError: Glacier exceeds domain boundaries` in shorter
  10/40 km test domains. The driver's default is 5 km. This one-dimensional
  downstream-domain length is separate from OGGM's two-dimensional
  `cfg.PARAMS["border"]=320` grid-border setting.
- The extension is a synthetic numerical safety domain, not a mapped LIA/RGI
  main-flowline observation. It is therefore retained for numerical integration
  but excluded from the length observation operator. The Core audit field
  `ice_node_count` defines the initial LIA pseudo-flowline domain that is
  comparable with the registered length target.
- The long and short branches are 11.85/10.50 km at spin-up end. By 2000 their
  raw OGGM node-count lengths are 21.10/11.25 km. System 3897 has 258 initial
  LIA-domain nodes at 50 m spacing (12.90 km) plus 4000 downstream safety nodes.
  The long branch contains ice thicker than 10 m beyond node 257, whereas the
  short branch does not leave the initial observation domain.
- The chain runner and controller now enforce a hard observation-domain gate.
  At every saved state they preserve raw OGGM length and compute the
  observation-domain length separately. If ice thickness exceeds 10 m anywhere
  downstream of `ice_node_count`, `observation_domain_overflow=true`, the
  observation length is undefined, all length errors/objectives are set to
  `NaN`, and the controller returns
  `acceptance_state=observation-domain-overflow`. The model state is not clipped
  and the raw geometry remains available for diagnosis.
- Read-only rescoring confirms that 3897/`delta_t=+0.875 K` is now hard-rejected:
  its raw peak and year-2000 length remain 21.10 km, but its observation length
  and objective are undefined. The `delta_t=+1.0 K` branch has no overflow and
  remains valid for ordinary length scoring; its forward peak/year-2000 lengths
  are 11.50/11.25 km.
- Regression tests for direct overflow detection, legacy-timeseries inference,
  and controller hard rejection pass together with the existing controller
  tests: 8 tests passed on 2026-08-13 using
  `D:\\Anaconda\\envs\\oggm_env2\\python.exe`.
- No new length-scored parameter expansion is permitted until all saved Core-191
  chains have been read-only rescored with this gate. If overflow is rare, only
  affected systems require spatially meaningful downstream-domain reconstruction.
  If it is widespread, the Core-191 downstream geometry must be rebuilt before
  rerunning affected systems. Chains without overflow can continue through the
  declared three-layer parameter loop.
- Reusable code and evidence:
  `Himalaya_greatGlacier/With_Rec_climate_organized/ice_surface_reconstruction/drivers/lia_observation_domain.py`,
  `Himalaya_greatGlacier/With_Rec_climate_organized/ice_surface_reconstruction/drivers/lia_lhs_single_chain.py`,
  `Himalaya_greatGlacier/With_Rec_climate_organized/ice_surface_reconstruction/drivers/lia_191_controller.py`,
  and
  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/lia_191_controller_v1/diagnostics/3897_b_branch_geometry_v1/`.
- The first complete read-only audit covered all 13 score sources currently

## 28. Northern PAGES early-event common-mode audit (2026-08-15)

- The fixed positive-`b2` network contains 50 records at 47 exact sites. All
  47 generic PAGES2k records were uniquely mapped through
  `combined_proxydata6.mat` to the 692-column reconstruction PAGES matrix,
  then to the official 692-column annual matrix and full TS metadata. The
  minimum correlation in both sequence-mapping stages is effectively 1.0 and
  the maximum affine residual is `1.33e-15`; all source hashes are unchanged.
- The mapped PAGES records are all tree-ring width (`TRW`) records interpreted
  as positive temperature responses. Forty are marked `Summer`, six annual,
  and one April-September. Species, genus, measurement material, and
  measurement method are empty for all 47 records in the available TS
  archive, so no species-family deletion is authorized or inferable from
  these files.
- The negative `1915-1918 minus 1905-1914` proxy event is concentrated in two
  independent northern study batches: Cook records have mean `-1.250 z` and
  Shao records `-1.464 z`. Removing either study alone leaves the all-site and
  northern means negative. Removing Cook and Shao together leaves `-0.466 z`;
  removing all PAGES records at or north of 35 N leaves `-0.250 z`. This is not
  a single-author or duplicate-site artifact.
- In both Berkeley/clean-GPCC and CRU/clean-GPCC fixed linear PSM branches,
  Cook and Shao residuals are more negative than all 47 same-length
  `1941-2000` rolling pseudo-events. The one-sided empirical resolution is at
  best `1/48`. Cook instrumental amplitude transfer is `0.193/0.224` for
  Berkeley/CRU; Shao transfer is `0.036/0.017`. Temperature and precipitation
  components are both too small; cancellation between them is not the main
  cause of the amplitude deficit.
- A unique-0.5-degree-cell annual comparison gives full-coverage warming in
  both northern blocks for every fully covered observational product. The
  western block has five full-coverage products, all positive, with mean event
  change `+0.412 degC`. The eastern block has four full-coverage products, all
  positive, with mean `+0.117 degC`. Eastern GISTEMP is complete at only one
  of eight cells and is excluded from the full-coverage consensus; its one
  complete cell is also positive. `rec_ref` is positive in both blocks, while
  the current `rec_result` is negative in both.
- Monthly Berkeley and CRU tests rule out annual averaging as the sign-conflict
  explanation. Western JJA changes are `+0.650/+0.319 degC` and April-September
  changes `+0.796/+0.545 degC` for Berkeley/CRU. Eastern Berkeley gives
  `+0.062/+0.203 degC`; eastern CRU is effectively neutral at
  `-0.0019/+0.0033 degC`. No region-product summer mean is below `-0.02 degC`.
- CRU station support differs sharply: western cells average about eight
  stations and have support in all 14 target years; eastern cells average
  about `0.95` stations, and the weakest cell has support in only three years.
  Therefore the western Cook-region conflict is the stronger chronology/PSM
  nonstationarity diagnostic. Eastern early-observation sparsity remains a
  plausible competing explanation. The next bounded climate action is a
  Cook-region chronology/PSM temporal-stability audit; do not retune
  precipitation forcing from this event and do not treat either proxy batch as
  invalid without independent evidence.
- Evidence is in
  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_pages2k_fixed_network_metadata_family_v1/`,
  `climate_reconstruction_pages2k_fixed_network_study_batch_v1/`,
  `climate_reconstruction_pages2k_study_batch_pseudo_event_residual_v2/`,
  `climate_reconstruction_northern_pages_annual_temperature_products_v2/`, and
  `climate_reconstruction_northern_pages_monthly_summer_temperature_v2/`.
  No experiment accessed `1921-1939` or launched OGGM.
- The declared Cook-region temporal-stability follow-up is complete. In the
  existing annual bivariate 1940-1969/1970-2000 split fits, 11 of 15 Cook

## 29. Cook chronology source and moisture audit (2026-08-15)

- The fixed `data_author=Cook, E.R.` label contains 15 records from 13 sites
  and three publication groups; it is not a single-study batch. The 13-record
  `cook2012tree` group, one `ahmed2011the` record, and one `cook2010asian`
  Bhutan record must remain distinct in source-level interpretation.
- Fourteen Pakistan records all decline from the 1905-1914 baseline to the
  1915-1918 event (mean `-1.349 z`); the 13 Cook-2012 records are also all
  negative (mean `-1.324 z`). BT018 in Bhutan is the only positive record
  (`+0.131 z`). The 15-record calibration PC1 explains 51.96% of variance,
  and 73.26% of the target event-vector energy lies along that PC1. The
  Pakistan decline is therefore a coherent archived chronology event, not a
  single-record artifact, but the correlation structure reduces the effective
  information to roughly 2-3 independent proxy modes.
- The 15 records map to seven independent early precipitation evidence cells,
  not 15. Only one cell has direct GPCC gauge support; it supplies the same
  evidence to PAKI029, PAKI030, and PAKI031. That cell gives clean-GPCC/CRU
  event changes of `-0.150/-0.291 mm/day`.
- Across all records, clean GPCC is negative at 15/15 and CRU at 14/15, so
  drying is directionally plausible. It is not a sufficient amplitude
  explanation: the BEA/CRU bivariate PSMs transfer only 19.3%/22.4% of the
  observed proxy event amplitude, while their precipitation components alone
  transfer 11.7%/11.0%.
- Decision: retain moisture stress as a hypothesis, not an established cause.
  Chronology construction and PSM temporal nonstationarity remain open. Do
  not delete the Pakistan records, force coefficient signs, or alter the
  production EnKF from this evidence. The next bounded action is to obtain or
  inspect chronology-construction information (sample depth, EPS/Rbar,
  detrending and chronology method) for the Cook-2012 source records before
  designing any operator correction.
- Evidence is in
  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_cook_chronology_source_moisture_v2/`
  and the evidence-independence correction in
  `climate_reconstruction_cook_chronology_source_moisture_v3/`. Inputs were
  unchanged; only 1905-1920 and 1941-2000 were read, `1921-1939` was not
  accessed, and OGGM was not launched.


## 30. Pakistan proxy information-weight sensitivity (2026-08-15)

- A frozen precipitation-EnKF replay tested whether the 14 Pakistan
  Cook-label records cause the 1901-1920 HMA precipitation decline through
  duplicate information weight. Prior members, observations, PSM operators,
  localization/background, RegEM diagonal errors, and all non-Pakistan
  records were frozen. The branches were archived baseline, explicit Pakistan
  ablation, and correlation-based diagonal-R inflation.
- The 14 records have mean 1941-2000 pairwise correlation `0.514`. The
  classical design effect is `7.688`, giving an effective count `1.821`; the
  spectral effective dimension is `2.925`. The weighted branch multiplies the
  14 diagonal R variances by 7.688 only as a sensitivity, not as a validated
  production error model.
- All numerical contracts pass: baseline closure `2.22e-16`, update closure
  `3.19e-16`, and explicit-ablation versus zero-gain equivalence `1.78e-15`.
- The hypothesis is rejected for HMA precipitation. Baseline trend is
  `-0.645 mm/day/century`; Pakistan ablation makes it more negative at
  `-0.799`, and correlation weighting gives `-0.742`. Both branches worsen
  RMSE against both CRU and GPCC. The corresponding 1915-1918 minus 1905-1914
  event changes are `-0.0856`, `-0.0992`, and `-0.0949 mm/day`.
- Therefore the Pakistan group offsets part of the negative HMA precipitation
  trend in the simultaneous EnKF update; it is not the duplicate-weight source
  of that trend. Do not delete or downweight this group from this evidence.
  The remaining mechanism lies in other positive-b2 records or the broader
  operator/covariance structure. This result concerns the precipitation EnKF
  only and does not diagnose the temperature reconstruction.
- Evidence is in
  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_precipitation_pakistan_group_weight_sensitivity_v1/`.
  Original inputs were unchanged, only 1901-1920 and 1941-2000 were read,
  `1921-1939` was not accessed, and OGGM was not launched.

## 31. Positive-b2 source-block EnKF ablation (2026-08-15)

- A frozen precipitation-EnKF replay partitioned all 60 archived-significant
  positive-`b2` records into three mutually exclusive blocks: 14 Pakistan
  records, 13 Shao records, and 33 other positive-`b2` records. Their union is
  exactly the full 60-record group. Prior members, observations, archived PSM
  operators, diagonal RegEM errors, and all nonablated records were frozen.
- Numerical contracts pass: baseline closure is `2.22e-16`, the all-positive-
  `b2` branch matches the earlier full-group result to `4.44e-16`, update
  closure is `3.19e-16`, and explicit record removal matches zero operator gain
  to `1.78e-15`.
- The baseline 1901-1920 HMA precipitation trend is
  `-0.645 mm/day/century`. Removing Pakistan makes it more negative at
  `-0.799` (shift `-0.154`), confirming that Pakistan offsets part of the
  decline. Removing Shao gives `-0.487` (shift `+0.158`) and improves RMSE
  against both CRU and GPCC. Removing the other 33 gives `-0.445` (shift
  `+0.200`), improving CRU RMSE but not GPCC RMSE. Removing all 60 gives
  `-0.216` (shift `+0.429`) and improves both reference-product RMSEs.
- The largest single-block trend effect is therefore in the heterogeneous
  other-33 block, while Shao provides the cleaner dual-reference improvement.
  The sum of separate block shifts is only `+0.203`, versus `+0.429` for the
  joint removal; nonadditivity is `+0.226 mm/day/century`. Do not treat block
  effects as additive or infer individual proxy causality, because the EnKF
  gain changes when records are removed.
- This is a mechanism-localization result only. It does not authorize deleting
  Shao or other records or modifying the production reconstruction. The next
  climate action should diagnose the heterogeneous other-33 block at a small
  number of physically defined regional/source strata, while retaining Shao
  as a separate documented sensitivity. Evidence is in
  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_precipitation_positive_b2_source_block_ablation_v1/`.

  zero operator gain to `1.78e-15`.

  longitude blocks shifts the trend by `+0.064` for `<80E`, `+0.061` for
  `80-90E`, `+0.075` for `90-100E`, and `-0.022` for `>=100E`. The joint
  33-record removal shifts it by `+0.200`. Regional effects sum to `+0.178`,

## 33. Early precipitation reference station/gauge support audit (2026-08-15)

- A read-only full-grid audit combined the stored 1901-1920 CRU, GPCC-derived,
  and `rec_result` annual precipitation fields with raw monthly CRU `stn` and
  GPCC `numgauge`, `infilled_numgauges`, and interpolation-error fields. Only
  1901-1920 and the 1961-1990 anomaly reference were read; the locked
  1921-1939 period was not accessed. Original inputs were unchanged and no
  EnKF, MATLAB, or OGGM run was launched.
- The raw precipitation month-to-year candidates correlate strongly with the
  stored fields (`0.984` for CRU and `0.939` for GPCC at best) but do not close
  exactly. Therefore raw monthly precipitation values are not substituted for
  the stored reference products. The raw files are used only for their direct
  station/gauge support diagnostics on exact matching 0.5-degree coordinates.
- Among 1705 cells with complete stored CRU, GPCC, and `rec_result` values for
  all 20 years, only 70 cells, or 4.22% of the jointly complete area, have both
  CRU stations and direct GPCC gauges in at least half of all months. Eighty-
  five cells, or 5.06% of area, have at least one directly supported month in
  both products. Seven hundred thirty-three cells, or 43.08% of area, have no
  direct CRU station and no direct GPCC gauge in any 1901-1920 month. Early
  gridded reference coverage is therefore highly interpolation-dependent and
  cannot be treated as uniform HMA observational truth.
- On the 70 dual-high cells, CRU and GPCC trends are `+0.535` and
  `+0.838 mm/day/century`, while `rec_result` is
  `-2.246 mm/day/century`; it lies outside the annual CRU-GPCC bounds in 17 of
  20 years. On the broader 85-cell dual-any mask, the corresponding trends are
  `+0.208`, `+0.552`, and `-2.079`. Thus the strong negative reconstruction
  trend persists, and becomes larger, on the limited area with direct support.
- Decision: early CRU/GPCC sparsity is a major limitation for HMA-wide
  validation, but it does not explain the opposite-sign `rec_result` behavior
  in the best-supported cells. Do not use full-domain CRU/GPCC agreement as a
  hard correction target, and do not dismiss the reconstruction conflict as
  reference sparsity alone. The next bounded action should compare the
  reconstruction and reference trends within fixed geographic regions while
  holding the same direct-support mask, to separate support selection from
  regional climate structure.
- Evidence is in
  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_precipitation_reference_gauge_support_1901_1920_v1/`.


## 34. Fixed-support precipitation longitude audit (2026-08-15)

- A read-only follow-up held the direct-support masks and the pre-existing
  longitude bands fixed while comparing stored CRU, GPCC, and `rec_result`
  annual precipitation for 1901-1920. No locked 1921-1939 value was accessed,
  original inputs were unchanged, and no EnKF, MATLAB, or OGGM run was
  launched.
- Dual-any support is strongly western: the bands west of 80 E, 80-90 E, and
  90-100 E contain 67, 11, and seven cells, respectively; the band at or east
  of 100 E contains none. West of 80 E therefore supplies 67/85 (78.8%) of
  dual-any cells and 56/70 (80.0%) of dual-high cells.
- On dual-any cells, CRU/GPCC/`rec_result` trends are respectively
  `-0.138/+0.263/-2.742` west of 80 E,
  `+1.529/+2.137/+0.060` at 80-90 E, and
  `+1.255/+0.709/+0.526 mm/day/century` at 90-100 E.
- Therefore the negative aggregate supported-cell reconstruction trend is
  west-dominated. Only the western reconstruction trend is negative; the
  central and eastern trends are positive. However, in all three supported
  bands with at least five cells, the reconstruction trend is more negative
  than both reference-product trends. The robust regional diagnosis is a
  relative-trend/amplitude under-response, not a negative trend in every
  longitude band.
- The V1 numerical tables remain valid, but its label
  `negative_reconstruction_trend_persists_across_supported_longitude_bands`
  is superseded by the corrected V2 classification
  `reconstruction_trend_more_negative_than_both_references_in_all_supported_bands`.
  This does not validate either reference product or authorize a production
  correction; eastern sample sizes remain small.
- Evidence is in
  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_precipitation_reference_support_by_longitude_1901_1920_v2/`.

## 36. Precipitation rec_result ensemble-definition correction and member decomposition (2026-08-15)

- The archived 0.5-degree variable `pr_ensemble_mean_rec_result` is not one
  EnKF experiment. The NetCDF builder first selects six median rec_result
  fields, `AO/HGAO/O` crossed with proxy networks `6/9`, and then takes
  their equal-weight finite-value mean.
- This corrects the scope of section 35. Its recovered prior/posterior closure
  remains numerically valid for `proxy6 / ordinary EnKF / experiment 1`,
  but that single native-grid experiment cannot be used as the prior/update
  decomposition of the six-median archived ensemble. The subsequent
  innovation/gain audit is likewise retained only as a single-experiment
  mechanism result: all 202 proxies are active and its gain is stationary in
  1901-1920, but it does not decompose the production-facing ensemble.
- A direct six-member audit reproduces the archived ensemble with maximum
  gridcell error `5.96e-08 mm/day`; fixed-support regional curves and trends
  also close to floating-point precision. Original files were unchanged, only
  1901-1920 was analyzed, the locked 1921-1939 period was not accessed, and
  no EnKF, MATLAB, or OGGM run was launched.
- West of 80 E, all six members are negative, spanning
  `-3.050` to `-2.480 mm/day/century`; the ensemble trend is
  `-2.742`. The western decline is therefore common across methods and both
  proxy networks, with proxy9 somewhat more negative on average
  (`-2.940`) than proxy6 (`-2.545`).
- At 80-90 E, all three proxy6 members are positive
  (`+0.655/+1.158/+1.237`), while all three proxy9 members are negative
  (`-0.849/-0.944/-0.898 mm/day/century`). Their network means are
  `+1.017` and `-0.897`, so equal-weight cancellation produces the weak
  ensemble trend `+0.060`. This is a proxy-network conflict, not a uniformly
  weak response shared by AO, HGAO, and ordinary EnKF.
- At 90-100 E, five of six members are positive. Proxy6 averages
  `+0.104`, proxy9 averages `+0.949`, and the ensemble is
  `+0.526 mm/day/century`; only AO_6 is slightly negative at `-0.076`.
- Decision: the production-facing regional diagnosis must be performed at the
  six-member ensemble level. The western decline is a cross-network common
  mode, while the central weak trend is created by proxy6/proxy9 cancellation.
  The next bounded climate action is a network-level proxy6 versus proxy9
  composition/operator audit in the central band, preserving method and source
  identities and avoiding record deletion.
- Evidence is in
  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_precipitation_rec_result_ensemble_member_decomposition_1901_1920_v1/`.

## 38. Climate reconstruction improvement loop rounds 00-02 (2026-08-15)

- A production-oriented climate improvement loop was opened. The active target is an independently versioned, reproducible HMA temperature and precipitation reconstruction; narrow diagnostics may continue only when they change a production candidate decision. Original source and legacy product files remain read-only, OGGM is excluded from climate tuning, 1901-1920 is diagnostic-only, and 1921-1939 remains a locked final test.
- Round 00 traced 12 source 0.5-degree median GeoTIFFs (temperature and precipitation, AO/HGAO/O crossed with proxy networks 6/9) to the archived NetCDF over the 982 currently allowed years 1000-1920 and 1940-2000. Maximum source-to-member error on source-valid values is `4.0054e-06`; network and six-member ensemble means close to `1.1921e-07`. All declared sources were unchanged and no locked value was read.
- Round 00 also confirmed a legacy output-encoding defect: 1630 of 3354 cells are source nodata (`-9999`) but become finite zero after the old anomaly calculation. The same classification holds for all 12 members. Those cells are outside the existing 1581-cell HMA mask, so the archived HMA score domain is not directly contaminated. A source-valid mask is now mandatory for all later scoring and v2 output must preserve nodata rather than encode it as zero.
- Round 01 froze a common-mask 1940-2000 temporal-block baseline for the six legacy members. The equal-six median region/reference RMSE is `0.46876 degC` for temperature and `0.29275 mm/day` for precipitation at field level; its median regional annual-mean RMSE is `0.30303 degC` and `0.12449 mm/day`. AO_9 is the best individual legacy branch for both variables, but its field-RMSE gains over equal weighting are only about 4.1% for temperature and 2.5% for precipitation. These are calibration-period control scores, not OOF promotion evidence.
- The Round 02 bounded composition screen used five 1940-2000 outer time blocks and compared the equal-six control with proxy9 mean, AO network mean, and training-block-fitted nonnegative stacking. Temperature has no passing variant. For precipitation, AO network mean improves median regional annual-mean RMSE by 6.43% with no region/reference regression; nonnegative stacking improves it by 7.83% with no regression.
- The precipitation stacking weights collapse to AO_9 in the first four folds and to AO_9/AO_6 weights 0.792/0.208 in the fifth. Therefore the result supports a simple AO-dominant precipitation candidate rather than a complex weighting model. Because the six base members were themselves calibrated over 1940-2000, this screen authorizes only a full PSM/operator-level OOF confirmation; it does not promote a production reconstruction.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v1/round_00_production_reproduction/`, `round_01_blocked_cv_baseline/`, and `round_02_network_operator_repair/`. The next active round is Round 03, restricted to operator-level OOF confirmation of the AO-dominant precipitation candidate against the equal-six control.

## 44. Climate reconstruction loop Round 03 and downstream closure (2026-08-15)

- Round 03 completed a true operator-level blocked test of the precipitation `AO_9` candidate over the allowed 1940-2000 instrumental domain. The five held-out blocks were 1940-1951, 1952-1963, 1964-1975, 1976-1987, and 1988-2000. No 1921-1939 values were accessed.
- The proxy9 full-calibration PSM closes against the audited official baseline to `1.7763568394002505e-15`. A replay of the historical AO index path confirms identical allowed-period observations but exposes an unrecovered PSM-version difference: maximum `HXb` difference `0.1496978523`; selected-member overlap is at least 97/100 per year and median 99/100. Historical index identity is therefore documented but is not used as the OOF acceptance gate.
- On the common 2-degree grid against CRU and GPCC across HMA, west, central, and east regions, the legacy equal-six control has median regional/reference annual RMSE `0.1278117465 mm/day`. The full-calibration AO_9 experiment-1 branch has `0.1329759912 mm/day` (`-4.041%` improvement). The blocked operator-OOF AO_9 branch has `0.1413487566 mm/day` (`-10.591%` improvement), with maximum pair regression `16.327%`.
- AO_9 therefore fails both frozen Gate 3 rules: it does not improve median RMSE by at least 5%, and it exceeds the 5% regional/reference no-regression limit. The AO_9 production candidate is closed; the legacy equal-six product remains the control.
- Because no candidate passed Gate 3, Round 04 is closed without a 50-pool full reconstruction, Gate 5A is not eligible, the 1921-1939 final test remains sealed despite prior user authorization, and Round 06 records `no_release` for `HMA_reconstruction_v2`. This is a scientific gate outcome, not an execution pause.
- All declared input sources remained unchanged. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v1/round_03_nested_ensemble_selection/`, `round_04_frozen_full_reconstruction/`, `round_05_validation/`, and `round_06_release/`.
## 45. Standard EnKF operator OOF closure (2026-08-15)

- A new independent loop-v2 experiment tested whether removing AO analogue-member selection recovers proxy9 precipitation skill. It used the same five 1940-2000 held-out blocks, the same blocked PSMs and residual variances, the same fixed experiment-1 prior pool, and all 500 prior members. The legacy equal-six and saved AO_9 OOF branches were recomputed as controls with exact score closure. No 1921-1939 values were accessed.
- The standard-EnKF median regional/reference annual RMSE is `0.1480120453 mm/day`, versus `0.1278117465 mm/day` for the legacy equal-six control and `0.1413487566 mm/day` for AO_9 OOF. Standard EnKF therefore worsens the control by `15.805%` and is `0.0066632887 mm/day` worse than AO_9.
- The standard-EnKF maximum pair regression is `34.069%`. The largest failures are east-HMA GPCC `+34.069%`, east-HMA CRU `+31.865%`, west-HMA GPCC `+25.337%`, and west-HMA CRU `+24.237%`. CRU and GPCC agree on the failure direction, so it cannot be attributed to CRU alone.
- Removing AO selection fails both frozen gates. AO selection is not the main cause of the operator-level OOF failure; it modestly reduces the error relative to standard EnKF, but neither branch is promotable. The current AO/standard-EnKF operator route is closed, and no 50-pool run is authorized.
- The next admissible repair family is upstream proxy9 PSM/observation calibration, especially fold stability of precipitation sensitivity, seasonality, and the relationship between proxy residual error and prior covariance. It must continue to use 1940-2000 blocked validation and independent CRU/GPCC scoring; 1901-1920 remains diagnostic-only and 1921-1939 remains sealed.
- All declared sources remained unchanged. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_00_standard_enkf_operator_oof/`.
## 46. Proxy9 PSM stability repair closure (2026-08-15)

- Loop-v2 Round 01 tested two upstream proxy9 PSM repairs under the same five 1940-2000 outer blocks and the same AO experiment-1 update. The bivariate ridge branch selected lambda independently for each tree proxy inside each outer training fold using inner blocked validation over the fixed grid `[0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100]`. The precipitation-only branch removed the temperature predictor for tree proxies. The seven non-tree proxies retained their existing temperature PSM.
- Strong regularization was selected frequently: across outer folds lambda `100` was selected 936 times and lambda `10` 328 times, while zero penalty was selected 97 times. This confirms substantial coefficient instability. Nevertheless, paired proxy-level holdout RMSE is nearly indistinguishable between ridge and precipitation-only fits, with fold median values near `0.90-0.98` standardized proxy units.
- Field-level validation rejects both repairs. The legacy equal-six median regional/reference annual RMSE is `0.1278117465 mm/day`; current AO_9 OLS is `0.1413487566`; ridge AO_9 is `0.1464803884` (`-14.606%` improvement); and precipitation-only AO_9 is `0.1488325665` (`-16.447%` improvement). Maximum pair regressions are `32.973%` for ridge and `27.135%` for precipitation-only.
- Ridge is approximately neutral in central HMA and improves central-HMA GPCC RMSE by `2.460%`, but worsens west-HMA CRU/GPCC by about `32-33%`. The precipitation-only branch worsens west and east HMA by about `24-27%`. Therefore a uniform HMA-wide regression-form repair is not acceptable.
- The PSM stability repair family is closed. Coefficient regularization and removal of the temperature term do not recover reconstruction skill. The next admissible mechanism is a predeclared spatial-support and proxy-error-covariance treatment, with regional definitions fixed before scoring; manual regional trend corrections and record deletion remain forbidden.
- No 1901-1920 or 1921-1939 values were used. All declared sources remained unchanged. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_01_psm_stability_repair/`.
## 47. Spatial covariance localization closure (2026-08-15)

- Loop-v2 Round 02 tested Gaspari-Cohn covariance localization with fixed compact-support cutoffs of `1500 km` and `3000 km` in the current proxy9 OLS plus AO experiment-1 blocked OOF branch. Localization was applied consistently to state-proxy and proxy-proxy sample covariances. PSMs, residual variances, observations, the fixed 500-member prior pool, and AO-selected 100-member sets were unchanged.
- Parent closure is exact: all `6100` AO local-member index entries across 61 years match the saved parent branch, the parent score difference is zero, covariance symmetry error is zero, and no linear solve required fallback.
- The legacy equal-six median regional/reference annual RMSE is `0.1278117465 mm/day`; unlocalized AO_9 is `0.1413487566`; the `1500 km` branch is `0.1387219840` (`-8.536%` improvement); and the `3000 km` branch is `0.1441278649` (`-12.766%` improvement). Maximum pair regressions are `15.491%` and `22.454%`, respectively.
- The `1500 km` branch improves whole-HMA RMSE against CRU by `7.375%` and against GPCC by `4.512%`, and is nearly neutral in central HMA. It nevertheless worsens west-HMA CRU/GPCC by about `14.8-15.5%` and east-HMA CRU/GPCC by about `9.5-12.5%`. The regional no-regression gate correctly blocks promotion.
- The spatial-localization family is closed. Long-distance covariance contributes to aggregate error but is not the dominant unresolved mechanism, and a narrower cutoff lacks support for edge regions. The next admissible mechanism is correlated proxy-error covariance or predeclared effective-sample-size treatment; manual regional correction and post-hoc radius tuning remain forbidden.
- No 1901-1920 or 1921-1939 values were used. All declared sources remained unchanged. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_02_spatial_localization/`.

## 49. GPCC calibration-target and gauge-support closure (2026-08-15)

- The spatial-localization family remains closed by explicit user decision; it is not the key unresolved climate-reconstruction mechanism and must not be reopened through additional radius scans.
- A new read-only audit resolved the precipitation loader identity again: the branch labeled `gpcp` reads GPCC Full Data Monthly Product Version 2022 (`mm/month`). The historical PSM source snapshot and preprocessing were not frozen, and the current raw file does not exactly reproduce the stored annual field. This remains a provenance and reproducibility defect.
- At the 290 precipitation-sensitive proxy9 records (127 unique 0.5-degree GPCC cells) over the allowed 1940-2000 calibration domain, monthly precipitation is complete for all 17,690 record-years. Therefore partial-year `nansum/12` behavior did not create the current calibration-period PSM failure.
- Direct cell gauge support is weak: only 35.881% of record-months have at least one direct gauge, 120/290 records have direct gauges in at least half of months, and 143/290 records have no direct gauge in any month. Median interpolation error is 7.13 mm/month.
- The legacy `nansum(monthly)/12/30` annualization differs from calendar-day annual means in absolute level, but after 1961-1990 anomaly centering the two series have median correlation 0.999978 and minimum correlation 0.999905. Median anomaly RMSE is 0.003705 mm/day (1.609% of the physical-series standard deviation); median century-trend difference is 0.001522 mm/day.
- Gauge support does not explain blocked PSM error. Direct-gauge fraction has weak positive, not negative, associations with ridge and precipitation-only holdout RMSE (record-level Spearman rho 0.124 and 0.122). No-gauge versus any-gauge ridge medians are 0.9449 versus 0.9887 standardized proxy units (Mann-Whitney p=0.121); the precipitation-only comparison is 0.9426 versus 0.9785 (p=0.092). Unique-cell associations remain weak.
- Decision: close direct-gauge record deletion/weighting and fixed-30-day correction as primary skill-repair mechanisms. Do not delete or downweight proxies solely from GPCC `numgauge`. Freeze a versioned, completeness-aware GPCC target for reproducibility, but do not claim this alone repairs reconstruction skill.
- The next admissible upstream test is cross-observational-product PSM stability: fit the same proxy network independently against GPCC and CRU precipitation under identical blocked 1940-2000 folds, then test coefficient sign/amplitude and cross-product prediction transfer before any EnKF rerun.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_03_gpcc_calibration_target_audit_v2/` and `round_04_gpcc_support_psm_link_v1/`. No 1921-1939 values were accessed, no OGGM model was run, and all source states remained unchanged.


## 50. GPCC-CRU cross-product PSM stability (2026-08-15)

- Loop-v2 Round 05 fit identical unregularized bivariate proxy9 PSMs against GPCC Full Data Monthly v2022 and CRU TS4.04 precipitation. The temperature predictor, 290 precipitation-sensitive proxy records, 1940-2000 observations, and five outer blocks were identical. No localization, proxy deletion, gauge weighting, EnKF update, or OGGM run was performed.
- Across 1,448 finite paired proxy-fold fits, GPCC and CRU precipitation coefficients have the same sign in 77.901% of cases, passing the predeclared 70% sign gate. Median within-product holdout RMSE is 0.9525 standardized proxy units for GPCC and 0.9513 for CRU.
- Replacing GPCC precipitation with CRU under GPCC-fitted coefficients changes median holdout RMSE by -0.022%; the reverse change is +0.385%. Both pass the predeclared 10% cross-product migration gate. Exactly 193/290 records (66.552%) meet the record-level four-of-five sign and bidirectional migration criteria, passing the 50% network gate.
- This is sign and prediction-transfer stability, not amplitude identity. GPCC-CRU precipitation-anomaly correlation has median 0.6519 and tenth percentile 0.3672; median target RMSE is 0.1529 mm/day. The median ratio between standardized GPCC and CRU precipitation effects is 1.649, while the 90th percentile is 7.553. Coefficient amplitude is therefore substantially product-sensitive for part of the network.
- All four frozen Round 05 gates pass, so a separately contracted operator test is permissible but not automatic. Because near-zero migration loss can also occur when precipitation contributes little beyond temperature, the next bounded action is an incremental-skill screen against a temperature-only PSM under the same folds and both products. Only a cross-product precipitation skill gain should advance to an EnKF operator test.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_05_cross_product_psm_stability_v1/`. MATLAB R2024b completed normally, all source states remained unchanged, and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 55. Incremental precipitation-skill closure (2026-08-15)

- Loop-v2 Round 06 compared the four Round 05 bivariate PSM paths with independently refit intercept-only and temperature-only controls over the same 290 precipitation-sensitive proxy9 records and five 1940-2000 outer blocks. No climate source was reread and no EnKF, localization, production reconstruction, or OGGM run was performed.
- Temperature-only itself does not improve the intercept-only control at network median: relative holdout-RMSE change is -0.163%, and only 47.465% of finite proxy-folds improve.
- The annual precipitation term adds negligible skill. Median relative RMSE improvements over temperature-only are +0.058% for GPCC fit/GPCC evaluation, +0.087% for CRU fit/CRU evaluation, +0.083% for GPCC fit/CRU evaluation, and -0.248% for CRU fit/GPCC evaluation. None reaches the frozen 1% practical threshold.
- Record-resampling 95% intervals cross zero for the first three paths and are entirely negative for CRU fit/GPCC evaluation. Improved proxy-fold fractions are 52.183%, 51.408%, 51.972%, and 45.563%, respectively. Only 95/290 records (32.759%) have positive median improvement in all four paths, below the 50% gate.
- All predeclared Round 06 promotion gates fail. Round 05 cross-product transfer was nearly neutral primarily because the annual precipitation predictor adds almost no blocked predictive information, not because GPCC and CRU define an amplitude-stable precipitation response.
- Decision: close direct EnKF/operator promotion of the current annual bivariate tree-proxy precipitation term. Do not continue with localization, coefficient regularization, product swapping, or post-hoc selection of the 95 positive records.
- The next admissible climate-reconstruction action is a proxy-network suitability redesign: classify records by archive, measurement, season, and documented climate response; define temperature and moisture proxy networks separately; then test moisture-capable records with nested cross-product validation before any precipitation reconstruction rerun.
- The v1 analysis completed all statistics but stopped during plotting because the installed Matplotlib did not accept `tick_labels`. The official v2 package copied the unchanged v1 statistics and regenerated only the plot/report with the compatible `labels` argument. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_06_incremental_precipitation_skill_v2/`; the v1 directory remains as an explicit technical-failure record. ## 61. Temperature-proxy association and temporal-stability diagnosis (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 09 reused the 214 independent documented-temperature identities, their Round 08 frozen seasons, the same 1940-2000 observations, and the same five blocked folds. It compared full-period association and in-sample skill with pooled blocked prediction, plus 1940-1969 versus 1970-2000 slope stability. No precipitation, EnKF, localization, OGGM, production reconstruction, or 1921-1939 value was accessed.
- The network median absolute full-period proxy-temperature correlation is 0.130 (record-bootstrap 95% interval 0.114-0.153). Median in-sample RMSE improvement over an intercept is only 0.853% (0.651-1.177%), below the frozen 1% threshold.
- Median blocked RMSE improvement is -1.243% (95% interval -1.565% to -0.884%). Early/late slope signs agree for only 59.624% of identities, below the frozen 70% stability threshold. Both the weak-association and temporal-instability flags are therefore true.
- The failure is not confined to one dominant proxy family. TRW (163 identities) and `trsgi_breit` (50) both have negative blocked median skill (-1.207% and -1.443%) and early/late sign agreement near 60% (60.123% and 57.143%).
- Full-period refit slope signs agree with archived temperature coefficients for 73.364% of identities but with formal documented response directions for only 48.598%. Existing Round 03 and Round 08 implementations use the same Berkeley Earth loader and nearest-grid mapping, and the earlier temperature-only baseline state closure is exact; there is no current evidence for a simple temperature-grid indexing error.
- Decision: classify the current documented-temperature linear PSM as weak and temporally unstable. Do not repair it by season switching, archive-family deletion, or coefficient constraints. The next admissible route is a complete HMA proxy-pool completeness audit based only on geography, formal metadata, and allowed-period coverage, followed by a separately contracted network redesign if additional eligible identities exist.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_09_temperature_proxy_association_stability_v1/`. All declared source states remained unchanged.

## 66. Berkeley-CRU temperature product attribution and local-PSM family closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 14 used the exact Round 13 214-identity LMR network, formal seasons, and five blocked folds to fit and cross-evaluate local linear proxy-temperature models with Berkeley Earth and CRU TS 4.04.
- The two local seasonal temperature targets are strongly related: median Berkeley-CRU correlation is 0.903. Paired fitted slope signs agree for 87.992% of record-fold pairs, so product differences do not explain the proxy relationship failure.
- Median fold-level RMSE improvements are +0.199% for Berkeley/Berkeley, -0.003% for Berkeley/CRU, +0.109% for CRU/Berkeley, and +0.492% for CRU/CRU. Every bootstrap interval crosses zero and neither within-product median reaches the frozen 1% threshold.
- Berkeley early/late slope agreement and formal-positive direction agreement are 61.792% and 50.000%. CRU gives 63.679% and 45.327%. Each product passes only the >50% positive-identity gate and fails the other four rescue gates.
- A separate closure recomputed Round 13 pooled-OOF metrics from the Round 14 Berkeley array. The selected-season arrays are exactly equal, and the maximum record-level metric difference is 9.89e-17. Round 13 and Round 14 numerical scales differ only because Round 13 uses one pooled OOF RMSE ratio while Round 14 summarizes fold-level relative improvements.
- Decision: close the current local linear temperature PSM family. Neither source expansion, formal seasonality, nor Berkeley-versus-CRU product choice provides transferable blocked skill. Do not continue coefficient constraints, product switching, or record-wise filtering.
- The next admissible mechanism is a separately contracted network-level regularized reconstruction proof: test whether collective proxy covariance predicts regional HMA temperature or precipitation under fully nested temporal blocking before considering a field/EnKF redesign.

Targets are unique-site regional means, so duplicate proxy sites receive no extra weight.

Neither reaches 5% RMSE improvement or correlation 0.30.

## 68. Purged low-frequency common-mode product split (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 16 tested an 11-year common-mode mechanism with outer blocks 1940-1959, 1960-1979, and 1980-2000. Test centers require their full window inside the held-out block; training centers and all standardization support are purged whenever their window overlaps the held-out block.
- All temperature branches fail strongly. JJA pooled OOF RMSE changes are -61.279% for Berkeley and -184.623% for CRU, with correlations -0.272 and -0.781. Annual changes are -89.071% and -83.895%, with correlations -0.485 and -0.455.
- The 22-record JJA moisture common mode splits by product. GPCC passes all gates: +7.043% pooled RMSE improvement, correlation 0.520, and improvement in 3/3 blocks. CRU fails: -32.879% improvement, correlation -0.038, and improvement in 1/3 blocks.
- Because the frozen mechanism requires both independent products, no family advances and no spatial-field or EnKF test is authorized. The GPCC-only pass is evidence of possible low-frequency moisture information, not acceptance.
- Decision: next audit the GPCC/CRU unique-site JJA targets themselves at 11-year scale, including phase/trend disagreement and direct gauge/station support over 1940-2000. Do not tune proxy weights or select records until the instrumental target conflict is classified.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_16_purged_low_frequency_common_mode_v1/`. All source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.
## 69. GPCC-CRU low-frequency target-agreement closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 17 compared GPCC v2022 and CRU TS 4.04 JJA precipitation directly at the 21 unique moisture-network sites over 1940-2000. It used no proxy fit, proxy weighting, EnKF, localization, OGGM, or production reconstruction.
- The unique-site regional annual and centered 11-year GPCC-CRU correlations are 0.688 and 0.765. Median site-level correlations are 0.743 annually and 0.816 at 11-year scale.
- In the three leakage-free low-frequency evaluation periods inherited from Round 16, GPCC and CRU trend signs agree in 1945-1954 and 1985-1995 and disagree only in 1965-1974. This is one disagreement out of three, below the frozen product-limitation threshold.
- Decision: the Round 16 GPCC-only pass is not explained by a material network-wide GPCC-CRU target conflict. Classify it as instability of the current proxy common-mode/model combination. Do not launch a raw gauge/station-support audit solely from this result, do not declare CRU inaccurate, and do not post-hoc select records or products.
- The expanded 22-record moisture network has now failed transferable validation under local linear, annual regularized-network, and simple purged 11-year common-mode mechanisms. Close those mechanism families before any production reconstruction or EnKF redesign.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_17_gpcc_cru_low_frequency_target_disagreement_v1/`. All source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.
## 70. Nested one-year alignment closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 18 tested climate-year offsets -1/0/+1 for the exact Round 14 temperature and Round 12 moisture networks. Offset selection was nested inside each outer training split; validation blocks lost their edge years and training excluded a one-year buffer so shifted predictors could not cross held-out boundaries.
- For temperature, all four Berkeley/CRU fit/evaluation paths have median RMSE improvement exactly 0.000% over zero offset. Only 24/214 identities improve on all four paths, and paired Berkeley/CRU offset choices agree in 67.422% of record-fold cases.
- For moisture, median improvements are +0.371% for GPCC/GPCC, 0.000% for GPCC/CRU, 0.000% for CRU/GPCC, and +0.166% for CRU/CRU. Bootstrap intervals are not strictly positive, and only 7/22 identities improve on all four paths. Paired GPCC/CRU offset choices agree in 74.757% of cases.
- Decision: close simple one-year climate/proxy misalignment as a network-wide repair. Do not change chronology labels or production operators from selected record-wise offsets, and do not continue lag tuning without a distinct biological-memory hypothesis and independent evidence.
- Together with Rounds 08-17, this leaves no validated local-linear, regularized-network, simple low-frequency-common-mode, instrumental-product-switching, or one-year-alignment repair for the current source-native HMA proxy networks. Any next production route must change the evidence base or reconstruction target/design rather than tune these closed mechanisms.
- Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_18_nested_year_alignment_v1/. All source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 78. Temperature increment scalar-feasibility closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 26 froze the ten Round 25 LIA backgrounds, increments, members, and four-family reference windows and tested whether one scalar multiplier could repair the assimilation update. It was a mathematical feasibility diagnosis, not calibration or an EnKF rerun.

Next decompose K(y-Hx) to determine whether the wrong direction originates in proxy innovations or the multivariate state-proxy covariance/gain operator.

Because whole-HMA held-out means are materially stronger than subregions, one final separately contracted regional-target test is admissible: fit and validate a scalar only on the HMA area-mean series and explicitly limit any passing product to a regional curve.
