- Eight records are independent new sites. Three annual wood-d18O records (`iso2k_1867`, `iso2k_272`, and `iso2k_745`) pass the frozen metadata and chronology gates; five records (`iso2k_1397` and four SISAL cave records) are admissible only as independent low-frequency validation evidence.
- Decision: advance only the three independent annual records to nested GPCC/CRU validation. New-site status and coverage do not by themselves establish PSM skill.
- Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_36_dod2k_hma_identity_chronology_admissibility_v1/. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 89. Independent DoD2k annual moisture PSM closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 37 evaluated `iso2k_1867`, `iso2k_272`, and `iso2k_745` in five fixed 1940-2000 blocks with formal seasons, a temperature-only baseline, and all four GPCC/CRU fit/evaluation paths.
- All three records have 100% documented-negative coefficient agreement and 100% GPCC/CRU fit-sign agreement. Their pooled three-record median incremental skill is positive on all four paths, ranging from +1.18% to +6.96%.
- No individual record passes every frozen stability gate. `iso2k_272` is closest but improves only 3/5 folds on the CRU-fit/GPCC-evaluation path; the other records fail two or three gates.
- Decision: do not promote the three records to an expanded annual PSM network and do not relax the 4/5-fold requirement. Directional plausibility is not sufficient evidence of stable predictive skill.
- Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_37_dod2k_annual_moisture_nested_cross_product_v1/. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 90. Co-located DoD2k measurement identity resolution (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 38 resolved the seven same-site cases at archive and measurement level. The v1 run exposed a label-compatibility issue (`Tree Rings` versus `Wood`); the preserved v2 correction changes only that normalization rule.
- Four wood-d18O records (`iso2k_1086`, `iso2k_1344`, `iso2k_503`, and `iso2k_556`) are distinct measurements co-located with Round 11 tree-ring-width records. Two cave-d18O records are likely existing measurements, and Dasuopu dust is a source-linked distinct measurement from the same ice-core dataset and is limited to low-frequency companion evidence.
- Co-located distinct measurements are not independent spatial sites. Decision: advance the four annual records only to a site-cluster-aware nested validation.
- Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_38_dod2k_colocated_measurement_identity_v2/. No proxy or climate numeric series was read in the identity audit.

## 91. Co-located annual DoD2k PSM closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 39 evaluated the four co-located wood-d18O records under the same Round 37 gates. The formal Oct-Sep season for `iso2k_503` was fixed to the ending proxy year; no lag was tuned.
- None of the four records passes every gate. `iso2k_1344`, `iso2k_503`, and `iso2k_556` retain 100% documented-direction and GPCC/CRU sign agreement but fail three, seven, and three skill/stability gates. `iso2k_1086` has 0% agreement with its documented positive direction and fails two gates.
- The initial preparation assumed all records contained 61 modern years and stopped before writing input when `iso2k_503` was found to contain the contiguous 1942-2000 interval. The preserved compatibility preparation represents 1940-1941 as missing without interpolation and changes no gate.
- Decision: close all seven newly audited annual DoD2k wood-d18O records as annual local-linear moisture PSM additions. Continue only with the independently admissible low-frequency evidence and do not infer annual reconstruction skill from modern coefficient sign alone.
- Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_39_dod2k_colocated_annual_nested_cross_product_v1/. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.



## 92. Independent DoD2k low-frequency interpretability closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 40 evaluated the five independent low-frequency records in twelve non-overlapping five-year bins over 1940-1999, using six held-out two-bin folds and all GPCC/CRU cross-product paths. Cave records used annual climate and `iso2k_1397` used its formal May-Sep season.
- No record passes all gates. The inferred coefficient orientation is mostly negative, but cross-product sign stability, held-out precipitation skill, or usable-bin support fails. Failed-gate counts range from six to ten.
- Decision: close the five records as calibrated low-frequency moisture validation proxies. They remain independent paleo records but cannot be assigned a stable modern precipitation orientation under the frozen model.
- Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_40_dod2k_low_frequency_interpretability_v1/. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 93. Pooled wood-d18O moisture PSM boundary (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 41 direction-oriented all seven Round 37/39 wood-d18O records from metadata and fitted one precipitation slope shared across records, with record-specific intercepts and temperature slopes. All fits and standardization were nested inside the five outer blocks.
- Four-path median incremental improvements are +2.31% to +3.53%; five of seven records improve on all four paths. The shared coefficient is wet-positive in 100% of fits and GPCC/CRU fit signs agree in 100% of folds.
- Three record-cluster bootstrap lower bounds are positive, but GPCC-fit/CRU-evaluation has a -0.29% lower bound. Therefore one frozen gate fails and the pooled class model does not pass.
- Decision: close the pooled wood-d18O local-linear PSM without leave-one-record deletion or gate relaxation. The first execution completed statistics but failed only on a Matplotlib keyword; it is preserved with suffix `failed_plot_compatibility`, and the compatibility rerun changed no scientific calculation.
- Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_41_dod2k_wood_d18o_pooled_psm_v1/. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 94. Raw public precipitation probabilistic-envelope closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 42 treated fixed HGAO, LMR, and O precipitation members as an unfitted three-member regional ensemble and compared held-out CRPS with an empirical training-climatology distribution for CRU and GPCC.
- The raw ensemble is severely underdispersed: full-period member-range coverage is only 13.1%-29.5% across HMA and three longitude regions, versus the frozen 35%-65% calibration range. Median block CRPS skill is -19.6%, only 25% of region/product blocks improve, and HMA improves in only 1/5 CRU and 2/5 GPCC blocks.
- Decision: close the raw public precipitation probabilistic envelope. A single nested spread-only calibration remained admissible because it changes uncertainty width but not the ensemble center.
- Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_42_public_precipitation_probabilistic_envelope_v1/. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 95. Nested public precipitation spread-calibration closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 43 fitted one nonnegative HMA-wide spread scalar inside each outer training block and transferred it unchanged to the other observation product and all subregions. The ensemble mean was never shifted or rescaled.
- Median fitted spread factors are 2.68 against GPCC and 3.09 against CRU, with coefficient-of-variation 0.146 and 0.140. Aggregate HMA member-range coverage improves to 45.9%-54.1%, and calibrated CRPS improves over the raw ensemble by about 8.8%-9.6% on all four paths.
- Despite calibrated coverage, every HMA path remains worse than held-out climatology: median CRPS skills range from -9.48% to -21.09%. Only 31.25% of region/product blocks improve and worst regression is 52.9%.
- Decision: close public precipitation spread calibration and the current public probabilistic target. The failure is not only underdispersion; the ensemble center/timing lacks sufficient held-out skill. Further precipitation progress requires an independent instrumental target such as APHRODITE or a materially different evidence source, not more member weighting, scalar tuning, localization, EnKF, or OGGM.
- Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_43_public_precipitation_nested_spread_calibration_v1/. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.


## 96. UDel precipitation allowed-period acquisition (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 44 acquired the NOAA PSL University of Delaware precipitation v5.01 HMA bounding-box subset through a THREDDS transport mirror that preserves the canonical NOAA dataset identity. The accepted v2 file contains exactly 732 monthly fields from 1940-01 through 2000-12; its SHA-256 is `cdb759317723ed9a566a8bcaefd18297ef0fc66e488d83051e35b0bc91866e9e`.
- The native 0.5-degree grid has 19.75-49.75 N and 55.25-115.25 E cell centers and nests exactly on the project target grid. Units are monthly centimetres and finite coverage is 94.3%.

- Decision: retain the strict v2 subset as an independent third allowed-period precipitation target. No 1921-1939 values were requested or accessed.

## 97. UDel/CRU/GPCC 1901-1920 precipitation audit (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 45 compared independently recentered UDel, CRU, and GPCC precipitation over 1901-1920 and tested UDel modern compatibility over 1940-2000.
- Whole-HMA UDel modern annual correlations are 0.586 with CRU and 0.742 with GPCC, but its 15-year correlation with GPCC is only 0.390 and fails the frozen 0.50 gate. UDel therefore cannot adjudicate the full-HMA low-frequency signal.
- Whole-HMA early trends disagree: UDel is +1.238 mm/day/century, CRU is -0.166, and GPCC is -0.063. The early full-HMA decline is not three-product robust.
- Regional signals differ. All three products decline in the west, are weakly positive in the centre, and increase in the east. This motivated a regional amplitude-support audit rather than treating the full-HMA mean as one coherent signal.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_45_udel_1901_1920_precipitation_product_audit_v1/`. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 98. UDel early regional-amplitude decomposition (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 46 decomposed the full-HMA early trend into fixed western, central, and eastern longitude regions. Their cosine-area fractions are 0.2555, 0.3098, and 0.4347, and the trend-contribution closure is 6.66e-16 mm/day/century.
- The west is the only product-robust early constraint. UDel, CRU, and GPCC trends are -0.723, -1.019, and -0.604 mm/day/century; all endpoint changes are negative, and UDel modern standard-deviation ratios are 1.054 relative to CRU and 0.934 relative to GPCC.
- Central and eastern early trend signs are positive across products, but UDel modern amplitude ratios fail the frozen 0.5-1.5 support interval and its early trend amplitudes are 6.1 and 24.5 times the CRU/GPCC means.
- Decision: retain only the western-HMA decline as a product-robust 1901-1920 observation constraint. The full-HMA direction remains unresolved.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_46_udel_early_regional_amplitude_decomposition_v1/`.

## 99. Fixed reconstruction western early-constraint screen (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 47 compared the six fixed public precipitation candidates with the Round 46 western observation envelope. Passing required the candidate trend and 1916-1920 minus 1901-1905 change to lie inside the UDel/CRU/GPCC envelopes and median annual correlation with the three observation curves to be at least 0.30.
- HGAO, O, local-EnKF, member-equal, and family-balanced candidates all pass. Their trends range from -0.761 to -0.984 mm/day/century and median observation correlations from 0.520 to 0.618. LMR fails both amplitude gates with a -1.161 trend and -0.192 mm/day endpoint change.
- Decision: these five candidates match the western early shape only; this does not establish modern predictive skill or a validated HMA precipitation field.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_47_public_reconstruction_western_early_constraint_v1/`. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 100. Western precipitation joint-validation closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 48 joined the five Round 47 early-shape matches with the frozen Round 31 western-HMA five-block CRU/GPCC scores. No fitting or climate-field rereading was performed.
- None passes all regional-curve gates. All have positive median block skill of 9.6%-11.8% and median annual/15-year correlations of 0.537-0.563 and 0.674-0.721, but temporal robustness fails.
- O is closest: 9/10 blocks improve and both products meet the four-of-five requirement, but one block regresses by 7.17%, above the 5% limit. Local-EnKF has no regression worse than 3.96% and 7/10 blocks improve, but CRU improves in only 2/5 blocks.
- Decision: early western agreement does not yet transfer to a validated modern western regional curve. Use the already amplitude-supported western UDel record as a fixed third-product diagnosis before requesting a new external dataset or changing reconstruction weights.
- The first execution completed all statistics but failed only on a Matplotlib boxplot keyword. It is preserved with suffix `failed_plot_compatibility`; the compatibility rerun changed no scientific calculation.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_48_western_precipitation_joint_validation_v1/`. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.


## 101. Western UDel modern adjudication (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 49 evaluated the five Round 47 western early-shape candidates against independently recentered UDel precipitation in the same five 1940-2000 blocks.
- All five pass the frozen UDel regional-curve diagnostic. Median block improvements are 12.9%-16.0%, annual correlations are 0.534-0.558, 15-year correlations are 0.649-0.745, and each candidate improves in at least four of five blocks without a regression worse than 5%.
- O improves 5/5 UDel blocks and 5/5 GPCC blocks, but its CRU path has one 7.17% regression. Local-EnKF improves 5/5 UDel and 5/5 GPCC blocks, but only 2/5 CRU blocks. Thus the Round 48 failures are product-specific rather than universal western candidate failures.
- Decision: keep the Round 48 gates unchanged and diagnose the exact observation-product conflict before any fourth-product adjudication. Do not promote a production field from UDel agreement alone.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_49_western_udel_modern_adjudication_v1/`. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

## 102. Western observation block-conflict closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 50 compared independently recentered UDel, CRU, and GPCC western-HMA series on 418 common cells in the frozen five modern blocks. A product was predeclared as a block outlier only when its RMSE to the other-product mean divided by the other-product pair RMSE was the largest and exceeded 1.5.
- CRU is a block-specific outlier in 1940-1951 and 1952-1963, but no product meets the outlier rule in 1976-1987. O's only severe regression occurs against CRU in 1976-1987, where the CRU outlier ratio is only 0.991.
- Therefore O's Round 48 failure does not coincide with a demonstrable CRU observation outlier under the frozen triad rule. Its good GPCC and UDel scores cannot justify relaxing the existing all-product gate.
- Decision: close O and the current fixed public precipitation candidates as validated western regional curves. Further precipitation adjudication requires a genuinely new independent product such as APHRODITE; do not continue weighting, scaling, localization, EnKF, or OGGM with the current evidence.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_50_western_observation_block_conflict_v1/`. Source states remained unchanged and 1921-1939 was not accessed.

- Decision: close HGAO residual amplitude shrinkage and do not proceed to a component-combination field.

## 117. Observation regional-to-spatial fingerprint closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 65 tested whether an observation-derived within-west spatial fingerprint can be predicted from the western regional mean. Cell loadings were fitted inside each training block and product, then evaluated only on held-out years and a different product.
- The 48 cross-product paths have -11.05% median residual skill, only 29.17% improve over zero, and the worst path is -57.51%. Every evaluation-product median is negative. Median annual spatial-pattern correlation is 0.131, but full-training product fingerprints have only 0.340 median pairwise correlation.
- Decision: close the single-regional-mean spatial-fingerprint mechanism. A validated regional curve cannot be converted into a gridded western field by this mapping.

## 137. External precipitation-product suitability closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 85 audited official metadata and access endpoints for APHRODITE, GPCC Full Data Daily v2022, CHIRPS v2, and REGEN against the frozen Round 84 requirements. No climate value, candidate field, or locked-period value was read.

- GPCC Full Data Daily v2022 is automatically accessible but is 1 degree for 1982-2020. Its official method interpolates daily relative anomalies and superimposes them on GPCC Full Data Monthly v2022 totals, which are already in the existing target family. It is not an independent replacement.
- CHIRPS v2 is automatically accessible at 0.05 degree for 1981 to near-present, but it is a satellite/climatology/station blend rather than an Asia-specific gauge product. Its official documentation explicitly warns that satellite estimates can be biased in complex terrain. It does not satisfy the frozen equivalence gate.
- The official Australian Bureau of Meteorology REGEN endpoint blocked automated access, so authoritative coverage and acquisition requirements could not be verified. Absence of verified metadata is not treated as a pass.
- Decision: no automatic APHRODITE-equivalent product is currently available. Continue only after an APHRO_MA V1101 file or authorized access is supplied, or after a separately approved scientific contract accepts a non-equivalent evidence family. Do not silently substitute GPCC Daily, CHIRPS, or an unverified mirror.
- Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_85_precipitation_external_product_suitability_v1/`.

## 149. Western 1901-1920 direct-temperature phase adjudication (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 97 compared the seven-station western GHCN-M network with the corrected six-member project reconstruction and the Round 21 family-balanced public reference. Products were sampled on the same public-grid station cells and used exactly the same station-year support; every series was independently centered, so the experiment adjudicates timing and trend but not absolute level.
- The observed network is robust: leave-one-country-out correlations with the full network have median 0.981 and minimum 0.906. Its 1901-1920 linear trend is +1.878 degC per century.
- The project six-member curve has annual correlation 0.047, centered RMSE 0.661 degC, negative RMSE skill -0.342, trend -2.789 degC per century, and nine opposite-sign years. Its trend is opposite to the direct station network.
- The family-balanced reference is closer but not validated: annual correlation 0.280, centered RMSE 0.476 degC, positive RMSE skill 0.035, trend -0.106 degC per century, and ten opposite-sign years. Its trend also has the wrong sign.
- The reference improves correlation by 0.233 and RMSE by 28.1% relative to the project, but it fails the preregistered trend-sign gate. Decision: the direct western adjudication is inconclusive between products; neither is accepted as a validated 1901-1920 western temperature curve. The evidence nevertheless confirms a material early-20th-century phase/trend failure in the current project ensemble.
- A source-grid latitude offset of 0.004881 degrees initially allowed an adjacent missing row to propagate into one public-grid station cell. The frozen data, metrics, and decision rules were unchanged; finite-neighbor bilinear weights were renormalized as recorded in EXECUTION_ADDENDUM.md. All source hashes remained unchanged and the result figure is nonblank.
- Advance to a frozen member/method/proxy-network attribution of the project ensemble. Do not tune against 1921-1939 or authorize production/OGGM forcing. Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_97_western_ghcnm_temperature_phase_adjudication_v1/.


## 150. Western early-temperature member attribution (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 98 sampled all six corrected project temperature members on the exact Round 97 western station cells and station-year support, then tested individual members, method composites, proxy-network-size composites, and every leave-one-member-out ensemble.
- All six members have the wrong 1901-1920 trend sign. Their trends range from -3.905 to -1.923 degC per century versus +1.878 degC per century in the robust station network. The best member, AO_6, has correlation 0.082 and negative RMSE skill -0.258.

- Decision: close nonnegative member weighting as a repair mechanism. A convex combination cannot reverse a trend shared by all six members. Route to their common reconstruction pathway rather than tuning ensemble weights.

## 151. Western early-temperature prior/increment mechanism (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 99 reused the verified Round 25 strategy-C recovery and decomposed each 1901-1920 station-support member as posterior = background + assimilation increment. It requested only 1901-1920 plus the 1961-1990 anomaly baseline.
- Component closure is 2.22e-16 degC. Recovered native posterior curves reproduce the exported-member curves with median/minimum correlation 0.9951/0.9936, so the mechanism result is not a replay or downscaling artifact.
- The station trend is +1.878 degC per century. The recovered six-member posterior trend is -2.435, its background trend is +0.702, and its increment trend is -3.137 degC per century. The increment has the posterior sign and equals 128.8% of its absolute negative trend, overwhelming a background that points in the observed direction.
- Both ordinary EnKF members have fixed zero-trend backgrounds and wrong-sign increment trends (-2.327 and -3.372 degC per century). Thus adaptive analog selection is not necessary for the failure. In 1917 the ensemble posterior/background/increment decomposition is -1.371/-0.122/-1.249 degC.
- Decision: the proxy-assimilation increment is the dominant and sufficient source of the early-20th-century western phase/trend failure. Keep prior replacement, localization, and member weighting closed; advance to station-targeted proxy innovation-times-gain attribution and then a network-wide PSM/chronology repair only if the contribution pattern is broad.
- All source hashes are unchanged, no 1921-1939 value was accessed, and the curve figure is nonblank. Evidence is in validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_99_temperature_prior_increment_station_decomposition_v1/.

## 153. Western early-temperature proxy contribution closure (2026-08-16)

- Loop-v2 Round 100 used all 50 archived ordinary-EnKF experiment pools and calculated innovation-times-gain contributions separately at every admitted Round 97 station cell before applying the exact station-year centering and network averaging.

- Negative and positive trend contributions are both large and opposing: -8.364 versus +6.028 degC per century in proxy6 and -8.579 versus +5.207 in proxy9. The net wrong trend is the residual of a broad mixed network signal, not a small bad-record subset.
- Decision: close record deletion, top-record ablation, and source-family deletion as repairs. Route only to a network-wide evidence/PSM/chronology decision; do not remove proxies based on contribution rank.

## 160. Cycle-1 Q1 monotonic multi-tributary structural closure (2026-08-16)

- The Q1 static preflight for system `3850` solved one joint monotonic constrained projection across all nine tributaries. The maximum and area-weighted mean absolute surface adjustments were 198.83 and 7.58 m.

The five-year 94.432 Mm3 artificial gain closes to the step budget and is dominated by 92.496 Mm3 from negative-section clipping plus 1.935 Mm3 from negative tributary handling.
- Decision: close the Q1 monotonic-regularized multi-tributary mechanism. Do not run a historical chain or promote it to the other Q1 representatives.

## 170. Cycle-4 joint LIA-state and delta-T EKI contract (2026-08-16)

- The user explicitly authorized a new joint state-estimation/parameter-estimation family after the Cycle-3 model-family boundary. Cycle 4 uses real OGGM evaluations in every ensemble generation; the legacy linear-surrogate `eki_curve_parameter_estimation.py` is not an admissible scientific implementation.
- The three-dimensional unknown is `theta=[q_V,z_shape,delta_T]`. `q_V` scales the uncertain V3/F19 initial volume over `[0.7,1.3]`; `z_shape` lies in `[-1,1]` and redistributes thickness longitudinally at fixed target volume; `delta_T` is centered on the system's current stable anchor over plus/minus 0.5 K and clipped to the existing global range. `melt_f`, `prcp_fac`, `glen_a`, `temp_melt`, `fs`, climate, window, bed, widths, `dx`, active LIA prefix, observation domain, solver, and formal score are frozen.
- Geometry uses analytic feasible anchors on the existing Core elevation-band axis, not SLSQP and not a true-mainline remap. The active-node length and area are unchanged, target volume is exactly `q_V*V0`, active thickness is positive, the surface is downstream-nonincreasing, and all safety-tail nodes remain ice-free. Volume is a prior state variable, not an observed target.
- Cycle 4 is LIA-state shooting, not conventional 500-1,500-year adaptive spin-up. Each candidate first passes static and 0.1/5-year zero-MB gates. A copy then runs for exactly 200 years under repeated 1441-1470 climate and the candidate `delta_T`; signed stability is `(V200-V0)/V0`. The historical 1470-2000 forward run starts from the unmodified candidate state, not from the shooting copy. This prevents the estimated initial state from being erased before the forward experiment.
- The EKI observation vector is `[L_peak,L_2000,signed_stability]` with target `[L_LIA,L_RGI,0]`. Endpoint whitening scales are `tau_i=min(0.2*abs(L_LIA-L_RGI),0.1*L_target_i)` and the stability scale is 0.02, so absolute normalized residuals at most one reproduce the unchanged separation, total-length, and stability gates exactly. Peak is the unchanged 1470-2000 observation-domain maximum; no peak-year or monotonic-growth penalty is added. Area/volume histories are recorded but do not enter the observation vector.
- A member is invalid on static or zero-MB failure, CFL/boundary/nonfinite/negative-section failure, or observation-domain overflow; invalid outputs are not clipped or imputed into ensemble covariance. Global OGGM concurrency remains at most 12. The default design is 18 members per generation and at most the prior generation plus three EKI updates (72 real chains), reduced to 12 members if the timing chain exceeds 90 seconds. An invalid fraction above 30% permits one prior-range contraction only; repeated excess invalidity closes the family.
- Before any ensemble, one timing/reproduction chain is released for system `3850` at `q_V=1`, `z_shape=0`, and `delta_T=+0.375 K`. It must separately record static, zero-MB, 200-year shooting, and 1470-2000 forward times and all hard gates. No EKI ensemble is authorized until this chain is technically clean and its `q_V=1,z_shape=0` geometry exactly reproduces the declared Core baseline.
- Representative selection for the three-system ensemble must exclude unresolved spatial-downstream task provenance unless its observation-domain geometry is explicitly rebuilt under this Cycle-4 state contract. Integer branch or task labels are not sufficient evidence of geometry compatibility.

## 186. Frozen-success baseline and continuous unresolved-system objective (2026-08-17)

- The project baseline is 22 formally accepted frozen systems plus 169 unresolved systems. The 22 accepted chains are immutable scientific results and are not rerun merely because a new structural mechanism is tested. The active objective is to resolve the remaining 169 by failure class and then assemble all 191 system histories.
- The final scientific deliverable remains the 1500-2000 volume evolution of all HMA LIA systems, with length as the primary endpoint validation variable and area/volume/MB retained as physical diagnostics. Parameter estimation, delta-T searches, and geometry construction are methods for state estimation, not the scientific endpoint.
- Continuous execution proceeds by class-level gates rather than per-glacier approval: one discriminating representative, three cross-class representatives, one ten-system batch, and then automated unresolved-system batches. Passed systems freeze immediately; failed systems receive a versioned failure class and are not silently skipped or individually hand-tuned. The full-chain target remains at least 85% completion before independent 1901-2000 validation and aggregated HMA comparison.
- For a physically routed synthetic-system model, zero-MB is a numerical conservation test, not a steady-length test. Its hard gates are volume drift at most 0.1%, no material negative-section or negative-tributary creation, no CFL/boundary/nonfinite failure, zero root-domain outflow, and a finite ice-free root boundary. Ice redistribution beyond the initially occupied nodes is recorded but is not itself a zero-MB rejection, because internal deformation can redistribute ice while conserving mass.
- Approximate LIA equilibrium is instead tested by exactly 50 years of the registered repeated B-window climate. Acceptance requires absolute total volume change at most 2%, final modeled length within 10% of the registered LIA length, at least 5 km of ice-free downstream domain remaining, and no numerical failure. The final 50-year state is the LIA equilibrium state used for the historical chain if it passes. A raw initial-domain overflow flag remains diagnostic; formal length is evaluated against the registered LIA target on the physically routed domain rather than censored at the initial occupied node.
- Section 185 remains the authoritative record under its former gate, but its observation-domain-only rejection is superseded prospectively by this clarified separation of numerical conservation and climate steady-state tests. The excellent `w181zero3850v2` mass-conservation result authorizes the exactly-50-year repeated-LIA-climate test for system `3850`; it does not yet authorize other systems.

## 196. Conservative one-way tributary FluxBased pilot declaration (2026-08-17)

- The exact zero-MB budgets identify a solver-level nonconservation mechanism: OGGM uses a negative tributary terminal flux in the tributary divergence update, increasing tributary section, but clips that same negative flux to zero when transferring mass to the receiver. The resulting artificial volume is measured exactly by `-min(Q_terminal,0)*dt` and closes the observed volume budget.
- One new solver pilot is authorized for system `2546` only, using its immutable `w194inv2546v4` inversion state. The solver inherits OGGM FluxBasedModel unchanged except for one conservative one-way junction boundary: after each native step, the exact artificial negative-terminal-flux volume is removed from the tributary terminal section, which is algebraically equivalent to setting an unsupported reverse junction flux to zero before the divergence update. No climate, MB, geometry, bed, width, thickness initialization, glen-A, fs, timestep, or scoring parameter is changed.
- The pilot runs only 0.1 and 5 years under ScalarMassBalance(0). It must record prevented negative-tributary volume separately, conserve total volume to 0.1%, leave no unresolved negative-section clipping or root outflow, retain finite nonnegative geometry and an ice-free root boundary, and close the corrected stepwise mass budget to numerical tolerance. It is a numerical solver experiment, not permission to fit curves.
- If `2546` passes, the same unmodified correction may be tested on `7`; `5537` remains excluded until a separate CFL-safe gate is declared. If `2546` fails, close the conservative-junction solver immediately and do not run other systems.

## 263. External proxy supplementation and annual low-rank closure (2026-08-18)

- Round 122 compares nine public external reconstructions with the allowed current field without reading 1921-1939. Long-period agreement is heterogeneous: northwestern-QTP precipitation has 31-year correlations `0.598` for 1500-1920 and `0.504` for 1940-2000, while eastern-HMA temperature benchmarks disagree strongly in some products. These curves are validation benchmarks, not fitting proxies.
- Four genuine public annual tree-ring d18O sequences were added to independent experiment storage: MiMei, Xinpu, Ganesh, and Keylong. Sequence-level closure confirms Ganesh and Keylong are not aliases of any current proxy9 record. All four show positive modern OOF precipitation skill in at least one annual PSM branch; Ganesh is strongest in the bivariate branch (`r=0.483`, skill `0.250`).
- Incremental global precipitation tests do not pass promotion gates. MiMei plus Xinpu worsen median RMSE improvement by `1.263` percentage points relative to Round 117. ## 265. Independent precipitation low-frequency validation of Xinpu/Keylong branches (2026-08-18)

- Round 133 corrected the spatial interpretation of the public QT-Prec benchmark before testing the Round 130/132 branches. The source paper defines the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau model-comparison area as 35-42 degrees N, 92-108 degrees E. Round 122's preliminary `east_ge90` comparison covered a much broader part of HMA; its reported 1500-1920 31-year correlation of 0.598 is therefore a coarse screening value and is superseded for formal NETP validation by the paper-matched Round 133 mask.
- The frozen comparison used baseline, combined Xinpu/Keylong BEA, combined Xinpu/Keylong CRU, and product-marginalized posterior fields. QT-Prec was area-weighted over 32 state cells in the published NETP box. The independent Shenqi Cave precipitation index was evaluated only as secondary isotope evidence against the nearest state cell to the published 28.93 degrees N, 103.10 degrees E cave location, namely 29 degrees N, 103 degrees E.
- Because the posterior state is annual precipitation while QT-Prec is May-July total precipitation and Shenqi is a monsoon precipitation index, the formal test used standardized low-frequency phase and trend direction rather than raw amplitude. It used only 1500-1920 and 1800-1920; no external series was interpolated.
- For QT-Prec over 1500-1920, baseline 31-year correlation is 0.2370. The BEA, CRU, and product-marginalized branches are 0.2406, 0.2408, and 0.2409. Over 1800-1920, baseline is 0.1401 while the candidates are lower at 0.1387, 0.1346, and 0.1368. Mean correlation changes relative to baseline are only +0.00110, -0.00082, and +0.00026, all far below the frozen +0.05 support gate.
- Shenqi correlations likewise change negligibly. The mean changes across the two periods are +0.00046, +0.00080, and +0.00069. All four branches preserve the same trend-sign pattern: agreement for both external records over 1500-1920 and disagreement for both over 1800-1920. Thus none repairs the nineteenth-to-early-twentieth-century low-frequency direction.
- Decision: close the current annual-Gaussian precipitation-assimilation route for Xinpu and Keylong. The records remain scientifically valid low-frequency constraints, but the tested operators do not provide independent evidence of improved precipitation reconstruction. Any future use requires an explicitly temporal/seasonal low-frequency operator and a new validation contract, not further innovation clipping, R inflation, or product selection on these branches.

## 279. Correction to the Hirpora western-causality interpretation (2026-08-19)

- The causal wording in Section 278 and `climate_reconstruction_temperature_warm_bias_west_anomaly_decision_v2` is too strong and is superseded here. The Hirpora experiment was numerically and procedurally valid, but its spatial interpretation was not sufficient for causal closure.
- Hirpora is a local June-July Kashmir reconstruction. The tested alpha branches are west-HMA (`lon < 80 E`) regional means formed by transferring ordinary-EnKF branch-minus-baseline increments to a six-member regional curve. Baseline standardization and low-pass smoothing do not make these spatial and seasonal targets equivalent.
- Independent western evidence is heterogeneous. Upper Indus and Hirpora have similar negative 1861-1900 low-frequency trends, while Kumrat has a positive trend. Their 1881-1900 baseline-standardized means are `+1.417`, `-0.113`, and `+2.057 SD`, respectively. The regional project curve is `+2.882 SD`.
- Alpha=0 remains consistent with Hirpora and Upper Indus trend shape, but it does not solve the Hirpora level mismatch: its 1881-1900 absolute mean error is `1.731 SD`. It also remains disqualified by the previously failed frozen uniform-alpha transfer gates.
- Correct decision: the archived regional warming is algorithmically produced by the temperature-operator covariance pathway, and Hirpora supplies evidence against treating that regional signal as universally representative. It does not independently prove that the regional covariance pathway is physically over-amplified everywhere or identify the unique physical cause.
- The western physical cause and validated correction therefore remain unresolved. The next admissible test must compare local or subregional candidate fields with co-located independent records under a frozen spatial contract. No production correction, EnKF replay, or OGGM run is authorized.

## 282. Eastern-HMA temperature trajectory extension (2026-08-19)

- Round 150 added the Eastern Tibet 2015 and Bhutan 2015 primary JJA series to the frozen Round 122 external benchmark without reopening a climate field. It reused only the allowed-year eastern-HMA regional curve and the original 1500-1920, 1901-1920, and 1940-2000 metric definitions.

- Over 1901-1920, both new products contradict the current warming trend. Eastern Tibet trends `-1.468 degC/century` and Bhutan `-3.449 degC/century`, while the current eastern-HMA curve trends `+0.426 degC/century`. Across all six annual external temperature benchmarks in the frozen comparison, only Sun 2026 has the same 1901-1920 trend sign as the current curve (`1/6`, or `16.7%`).
- This is not a general modern failure. Over 1940-2000, Eastern Tibet has raw/31-year correlation `0.574/0.762` and Bhutan `0.472/0.934` with the current curve; both agree with its positive trend.

The evidence localizes the disagreement to early-twentieth-century timing rather than invalidating the entire temperature reconstruction. The next admissible main-line test must attribute that timing to the instrumental target/prior versus proxy/operator pathway under a frozen experiment; do not return to localization, blind parameter scans, EnKF production reruns, or OGGM.

## 283. Early-20th-century temperature production-stage attribution (2026-08-19)

- Round 151 decomposed the current public eastern-HMA temperature curve over 1901-1920 into the archived six-member background, the EnKF assimilation increment, and a public spatial-export/resampling residual. It read only 1800-1920 and 1961-1990 from archived proxy/posterior sources; 1921-1939 and Jionglacuo remained unopened.
- The public eastern-HMA trend is `+0.42572 degC/century`. The reconstructed background contributes `+0.60461`, the EnKF proxy update contributes `-0.18707`, and the export/resampling residual contributes only `+0.00818 degC/century`. The native posterior trend is `+0.41754 degC/century`.
- Both annual identities close to `3.33e-16 degC`: native posterior equals background plus increment, and the public curve equals background plus increment plus export residual. The public trend also closes exactly to the Round 150 value.
- The positive eastern trend is therefore background-dominant. The EnKF update opposes rather than creates the warming, and the public export is negligible at this regional scale. This does not contradict earlier single-pixel export artifacts; it establishes that export is not the main source of the Round 150 eastern-HMA regional trend.
- The term "instrumental target" is not a separate annual 1901-1920 component. Berkeley Earth/CRU and other instrumental targets enter the archived workflow through 1940-2000 PSM calibration; their 1901-1920 values were not annually assimilated. Round 151 therefore cannot attribute the early trend to erroneous 1901-1920 CRU values.
- Member-level background trends identify the relevant algorithmic distinction. The ordinary O-EnKF background is fixed and has zero trend. AO/HGAO share adaptive strategy-C backgrounds: proxy6 contributes `+0.74208` and proxy9 `+1.07176 degC/century` before six-member averaging. No EnKF rerun or OGGM run occurred and all source hashes remained unchanged.

## 284. Adaptive-background support/value factorial attribution (2026-08-19)

- The first Round 152 implementation stopped before producing a result because the fixed-support/fixed-value control had one column rather than the required 20-year matrix. It changed no source. The proxy-value main effect is `+0.60457`; changing proxy support contributes only `+0.00521`; the support-value interaction is `-0.00517`; and the constant-pattern control is zero. It is not a raw transient trend in the fixed prior, a proxy-count discontinuity, the EnKF update, or the public export.

## 285. Adaptive-background proxy-group sensitivity closure (2026-08-19)

- Round 153 omitted one complete pre-defined proxy group at a time from the deterministic adaptive-background selection. Groups were frozen by longitude, temperature-coefficient sign, precipitation-coefficient sign, and archived PSM significance; overlapping families were reported separately and are not additive causal contributions.
- The dominant sensitivity is the proxy9 central-HMA group: omitting all 97 records at `80-90 E` changes the six-member eastern background trend from `+0.60461` to `-0.00916 degC/century`. The resulting warming effect is `+0.61377 degC/century`, or `101.5%` of the full trend. Thus other network components slightly offset this group-conditioned selection response.
- The next-largest longitude sensitivity has the opposite sign. Omitting the 80 proxy9 records west of 80 E increases the trend to `+0.99930 degC/century`, an effect of `-0.39469`. Within overlapping operator groups, proxy9 records with non-significant archived PSMs have a positive `+0.24875` effect, nonnegative temperature coefficients `+0.20882`, and negative precipitation coefficients `+0.15366 degC/century`; these overlaps do not uniquely identify a physical proxy class.
- This result does not authorize deleting the central proxy9 records. Their influence is through nonlinear strategy-C member selection, and a leave-out response is not an independent causal contribution or evidence that the records are wrong.
- Decision: the next admissible repair experiment is one predeclared spatially balanced adaptive-background selection operator, evaluated first by blocked 1940-2000 modern OOF and split-period stability. Do not replace CRU from this result, delete proxies, tune individual records, change EnKF gain/R, run a production reconstruction, open the sealed validation period, or run OGGM. Only a modern-passing balanced operator may advance to an allowed-period trajectory comparison.
- Round 153 reproduced the Round 152 proxy6/proxy9 background trends within `2.22e-16 degC/century`, accessed no locked or Jionglacuo value, ran neither EnKF nor OGGM, and left all tracked sources unchanged.

## 286. Co-located western-temperature heterogeneity closure (2026-08-19)

- A prospectively frozen comparison evaluated Hirpora JJ, Kumrat MA, and Upper Indus MAMJJAS temperature records against the nearest jointly valid native 0.5-degree project cell and an area-weighted 100 km HMA-cell mean. Nearest-cell distances are 21.2-27.8 km and each radius contains 9-13 jointly valid cells.
- The archived `alpha=1`, attenuated `alpha=0.25`, and zero transferred-covariance-anomaly `alpha=0` branches close algebraically to `8.88e-16 degC` or better. Nearest-cell and 100 km results give the same decision.
- `alpha=0` improves 1861-1900 RMSE by 49.3-49.8% at Hirpora and 32.7-36.7% at Upper Indus and reproduces their negative trend signs. At Kumrat, however, it reverses the independently positive trend from `+3.73` to `-3.56/-3.84 SD/century` and reduces correlation from about `+0.34/+0.35` to `-0.08/-0.07`; it fails the frozen joint gate at both scales.
- `alpha=0.25` passes the Hirpora and Upper Indus target gates but improves Kumrat RMSE by only 1.7-2.2%, below the frozen 5% requirement. Neither attenuation branch passes all six targets.
- Decision: close the uniform western-alpha correction route. The evidence supports spatial or seasonal heterogeneity, not one western-HMA covariance correction. Because the project field is annual while the independent targets use JJ, MA, and MAMJJAS seasons, this test cannot uniquely separate spatial from seasonal heterogeneity and does not identify a replacement operator.
- The experiment read no value later than 1900, changed no source, and authorized no production correction, EnKF production replay, or OGGM run. All tracked source hashes remained unchanged.

## 297. Temperature perfect-model twin and amplitude-recovery boundary (2026-08-20)

- Round 161 tested the archived temperature method independently of real proxy quality. Twenty-four deterministic truth members were held out from the experiment-1 500-member pool. Their exact full-PSM `HXb` values generated noise-free and five fixed-seed RegEM-residual-noise pseudo-observations for proxy6 and proxy9. Actual proxy observations and instrumental fields were not used.
- V1 stopped before any twin reconstruction because it paired the 14-by-24 prior state coordinates with the 43-by-78 instrumental-grid HMA mask. Independent v2 changed only the mask/coordinate source to the verified native arrays in `heldout_oof_fields.npz`.
- The equal-network ordinary EnKF recovers regional phase but not enough absolute state amplitude. In the noise-free condition, HMA median state RMSE is `0.3866 degC`, only `27.87%` better than the all-500 background; with RegEM residual noise it is `0.4163 degC` and `22.34%` better. The frozen noise-free minimum was `50%`, so the experiment fails one of seven gates.
- Top-100 adaptive AO is worse than ordinary EnKF in the same idealized test: HMA state-RMSE improvements are `24.39%` noise-free and `19.02%` with noise. Analogue selection therefore adds error even when pseudo-observations exactly obey the archived operator.
- Ordinary regional-value correlations remain high (`0.9647` noise-free and `0.9292` with noise), but the apparent HMA spatial-pattern correlations near `0.998` are not evidence of dynamic spatial recovery: the unchanged background itself has median pattern correlation `0.9975` with held-out truth members, showing that the metric is dominated by the common static prior pattern.
- Decision: do not release the instrumental-truth twin yet. First decompose anomaly amplitude, prior effective rank, and unresolved orthogonal variance under the same held-out truths. The result identifies a method/prior amplitude-recovery boundary before any claim about real proxy quality can be made.
- Round 161 accessed no actual proxy observation, instrumental value, 1901-1939 value, or Jionglacuo value; it changed no source and ran neither production reconstruction nor OGGM. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_161_temperature_perfect_model_twin_v2/`.


## 298. Temperature twin information-geometry closure (2026-08-20)

- Round 162 replayed the exact Round 161 perfect-model experiment and decomposed the noise-free ordinary-EnKF error into prior-state, observation-coupled, and actual-increment limits. It used the same 500-member pool, 24 disjoint held-out truths, full archived PSM operators, residual variances, seed, and native HMA mask.
- The sampled HMA prior is not the limiting representation. Its 105 positive-weight state cells have full numerical rank 105; the 99%-variance subspace has rank 52 and median oracle state-RMSE skill `0.8664`, while the complete prior span reproduces the held-out truth-minus-background anomalies to numerical precision.
- The practical observation-coupled geometry is much narrower. For the equal proxy6/proxy9 network, residual-standardized state/proxy cross covariance has median participation-ratio effective rank `1.6576`; only six directions contain 99% of its singular energy. Projection onto those six directions has median oracle skill `0.4186` and resolves `66.15%` of truth-error variance.
- The actual update is not merely too small. Its median norm is `0.5495` of the truth-error norm and its cosine alignment is only `0.6932`. The best case-wise scalar multiplier has median `1.2606` but raises median skill only from `0.2737` to `0.2801`. A uniform gain or temperature offset therefore cannot recover the missing state structure.
- The same separation appears regionally: prior-99% oracle skill is about `0.866-0.886`, while equal-network actual median skill is `0.343` west, `0.163` central, and `0.303` east. This is not a single-region failure.
- Decision: close scalar amplitude correction as the next remedy. The dominant perfect-model boundary is the low-dimensional practical observation-coupled subspace plus innovation-direction weighting, not inability of the sampled prior to express the truth. The next diagnostic must map prior temperature modes to residual-standardized PSM observability before any real-proxy reconstruction or bias correction is attempted.
- Round 162 used no actual proxy observations or instrumental values, accessed no 1921-1939 or Jionglacuo value, changed no declared source, and ran neither production reconstruction nor OGGM. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_162_temperature_twin_information_geometry_v1/`.


## 299. Temperature PSM mode-observability boundary (2026-08-20)

- Round 163 decomposed the frozen HMA prior and residual-standardized archived proxy operators mode by mode, using the same Round 161/162 500-member pool and 24 held-out truths. It made no selection, localization, gain adjustment, or bias correction.
- Six area-weighted HMA prior modes contain 80% of state variance. Mode 1 contains `43.07%` of prior variance but `74.86%` of stacked proxy6/proxy9 state-coupling energy, confirming strong common-mode concentration without establishing complete rank collapse.
- The stacked proxy-anomaly ensemble has participation-ratio effective rank `8.82`, while state/proxy coupling has effective rank only `1.71`; three coupling directions contain 90% and ten contain 99% of coupling energy.
- The first three prior modes remain materially observable: their exact linear-Gaussian posterior variance reductions are `0.862`, `0.771`, and `0.591`. Modes 4-6 are weaker and uneven at `0.355`, `0.511`, and `0.329`; modes 9-15 are mostly below `0.31`.
- Therefore Round 162's low practical gain-space skill is not a pure statement that all secondary modes are invisible. It combines overconcentration on the leading common mode with unequal residual-error shrinkage across otherwise observable modes. The next decisive perfect-model test is a frozen noise-free residual-variance (`R`) ablation, not localization or another scalar posterior multiplier.
- Round 163 used no actual proxy observations or instrumental values, accessed no 1921-1939 or Jionglacuo value, changed no declared source, and ran neither production reconstruction nor OGGM. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_163_temperature_psm_mode_observability_v1/`.


## 300. Noise-free residual-variance ablation boundary (2026-08-20)

- Round 164 replayed the exact noise-free perfect-model twin at residual-variance scales `1`, `0.25`, `0.0625`, `0.01`, and `0.0001`. These were diagnostic ablations, not production candidates or selected hyperparameters.
- The archived-R equal-network HMA ratio-of-median-RMSE skill exactly closes Round 161 at `0.2787`. Reducing R monotonically raises it to `0.4816` at scale `0.0001`, still below the frozen `0.50` gate. Residual-error shrinkage therefore explains most, but not all, of the idealized recovery deficit.
- Near-zero-R proxy9 reaches HMA skill `0.4909`, proxy6 `0.4453`, and their simple posterior average `0.4816`. The equal average is not better than the stronger network. Regionally the equal branch reaches `0.5707` west and `0.5470` east but only `0.4476` central HMA.
- Modal transfer confirms unequal rather than scalar attenuation. At archived R, equal-network slopes for modes 1-6 are `0.868`, `0.724`, `0.446`, `0.252`, `0.336`, and `0.254`; near-zero R raises them to `0.985`, `1.040`, `0.808`, `0.864`, `0.846`, and `0.864`, but mode-6 RMSE skill remains only `0.294` because its direction/case transfer is unstable.
- Decision: stop reducing R. The next perfect-model mechanism test must compare the current mean of two separately assimilated network posteriors with one joint proxy6+proxy9 assimilation. This tests information fusion directly without localization, real-data tuning, or a new PSM.
- Round 164 used no actual proxy observations or instrumental values, accessed no 1921-1939 or Jionglacuo value, changed no declared source, and ran neither production reconstruction nor OGGM. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_164_temperature_twin_residual_variance_ablation_v1/`.


## 301. Perfect-model joint-network fusion closure (2026-08-21)

- Round 165 compared the current mean of separately assimilated proxy6/proxy9 posterior means with one stacked 499-proxy update under the exact Round 161-164 noise-free held-out-truth design. Archived R and the predeclared `0.0001` diagnostic scale were tested without proxy selection, localization, or real-data tuning.
- Joint assimilation improves HMA ratio-of-median-RMSE skill from `0.2787` to `0.3095` at archived R, a gain of `0.0308`. At near-zero R it improves skill from `0.4816` to `0.49989`, a gain of `0.0183`.
- The near-zero joint value misses the frozen `0.50` threshold by only `0.00011`, so the threshold-edge distinction is not scientifically material. The substantive result is that network fusion contributes only two to three percentage points and cannot explain the large archived-R deficit.
- Regionally, near-zero joint skill is `0.5834` west, `0.4926` central, and `0.5535` east. Central HMA remains the weakest region even after both residual suppression and joint fusion.
- Decision: close separate-posterior averaging as a secondary inefficiency, but do not promote stacked assimilation. The stacked branch assumes cross-network residual independence that has not been established, and its archived-R skill remains only `0.3095`. Stop R reduction, gain scaling, network averaging/stacking, localization, and prior-member weighting within this archived temperature family.
- Round 165 used no actual proxy observations or instrumental values, accessed no 1921-1939 or Jionglacuo value, changed no declared source, and ran neither production reconstruction nor OGGM. Evidence is in `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_165_temperature_twin_joint_network_fusion_v1/`.


## 302. Archived temperature-family terminal decision (2026-08-21)

- Round 166 synthesized only verified Round 161-165 result summaries and the canonical facts contract. It ran no reconstruction and opened no climate, proxy, instrumental, locked-period, or glacier value input.
- The sampled prior can represent held-out truth (`0.866` practical prior-99% oracle skill), while scalar increment scaling, top-100 adaptive selection, residual-variance reduction, and separate-versus-joint proxy-network fusion all fail to provide a defensible production repair. Near-zero-R joint assimilation reaches `0.49989` only under an unverified cross-network residual-independence assumption; archived-R joint skill is `0.3095`.
- Decision: close the archived temperature prior/PSM/operator family for further repair. Do not run an instrumental-truth twin, production reconstruction, OGGM forcing, localization, R/gain tuning, prior-member weighting, or proxy6/proxy9 stacking from this family.
- The next admissible route is genuinely new raw temperature-sensitive evidence or chronology in central (`80-90 E`) or eastern (`>=90 E`) HMA, with central HMA prioritized. A candidate must be non-aliased raw evidence, have documented temperature interpretation/season, reach at least 1500, and provide at least 20 allowed modern observations over 1940-2000.

Until then, the six-member field remains legacy experimental forcing and the four-family product remains only an HMA regional 50-year comparison curve.

## 313. Eastern Tibetan Plateau external warm-bias audit (2026-08-21)

- Round 184 used the reconstruction-only Mendeley dataset
  `10.17632/s7t4zc34sr.2` strictly as independent low-frequency comparison
  evidence. Its target is eastern Tibetan Plateau June-September mean
  temperature, while the project and four-family curves are HMA annual means;
  this spatial-seasonal mismatch precludes field validation or direct fitting.
- On the eight complete 50-year windows from 1500-1549 through 1850-1899, the
  external reconstruction is colder than the project six-member curve in all
  eight. The median project-minus-external difference is `+0.197 degC`, which
  independently supports the direction of the diagnosed project warm bias.
- The external curve is not closer to the four-family central curve: its median
  absolute distance is `0.231 degC` from the four-family central estimate and
  `0.197 degC` from the project curve. It lies within the four-family range in
  only three of eight windows; 50-year correlations are `0.258` with the
  four-family central curve and `0.491` with the project curve.
- Therefore the strict two-part confirmation gate fails. Retain the warm-bias
  direction as independently supported, but do not interpret the previous
  `+0.383 degC` project-minus-four-family value as a validated global offset.
  A uniform translation to the four-family central curve is not authorized.

## 320. Dual eastern-HMA thermal-index transport result (2026-08-21)

- Round 192 prospectively combined the Hengduan and Haizi standard chronologies
  with equal weights after training-fold standardization. Their documented
  instrumental targets were likewise combined as a dimensionless local thermal
  index; it was never represented as a degrees-C HMA field.
- The five-block 1940-1999 OOF test passed every frozen modern gate. Berkeley
  Earth correlation/skill were `0.306/0.093`; CRU were `0.438/0.188`; positive
  fold counts were `5/5` and `4/5`, all ten fitted slopes were positive, and the
  two product predictions correlated `0.990`.
- Round 193 then applied the unchanged equal-weight index to 1500-1899 and
  compared only low-frequency shape with the partially source-overlapping Wang
  2015 trajectory benchmark. The dual index failed every historical gate:
  centered-31-year correlation `-0.111`, eight-window 50-year correlation
  `0.066`, and adjacent-window sign agreement `3/7`.
- The failure is diagnostic. Hengduan alone has 50-year correlation `0.573` and
  sign agreement `5/7` with Wang, while Haizi is opposite at `-0.342` and `2/7`.
  Combining them improves modern instrumental skill but cancels historical
  low-frequency shape. This is direct evidence that modern common skill does
  not guarantee paleo low-frequency transport across differently standardized,
  differently seasonal regional chronologies.
- Decision: close the equal-weight dual index. Do not tune weights, seasons,
  signs, lags, or thresholds against Wang. Its absolute temperature amplitude
  was never validated, and no EnKF, production correction, or OGGM is
  authorized. Both parsers matched their modern Round 180/183 exports exactly,
  skipped all 19 locked rows before value conversion, and left sources unchanged.

## 321. Wang Gongshan--CHIN041 lineage correction (2026-08-21)

- Round 194 establishes that Wang et al. (2015) Gongshan and NOAA CHIN041 are
  different collections. Wang Gongshan is the Fan et al. (2010) `Larix
  speciosa` DL1+DL2 regional chronology with 68 series and a reliable period of
  1585-2005. NOAA CHIN041 is the `Tsuga dumosa` `22DL_T_r` collection with 35
  dated series over 1530-2005.
- This corrects the inference path used after Round 190: the zero CHIN041 sample
  overlap in Round 191 cannot establish independence between Wang Gongshan and
  the new `Larix speciosa` DLL site. DLL lies in the same sampling region; the
  relationship remains unresolved until Fan 2010 DL1/DL2 raw identities are
  recovered or DLL is prospectively excluded and the chronology rebuilt.
- Round 193 remains scientifically valid as a failed comparison against a
  potentially locally source-overlapping benchmark. Because it fails rather
  than promotes the operator, the unresolved overlap cannot create a false
  acceptance. The dual index remains closed.
- No annual value, locked-period value, or Jionglacuo value was read in Round
  194, and no EnKF or OGGM run occurred. Evidence is in
  `validation_data/results/paleo_surface_validation_v0/climate_reconstruction_improvement_loop_v2/round_194_wang_gongshan_chin041_lineage_correction_v1/`.

## 328. Early-twentieth-century phase interpretation correction (2026-08-22)

- Round 207 v2 found that all six frozen project members have positive
  1901-1920 trends while Huang winter Tmin is negative. This establishes a
  project-common disagreement with Huang, not a project-common error. Round
  208 supersedes any stronger `wrong-sign` interpretation.
- Round 208 downloaded only the official CRU TS4.01 Tmin decade files for
  1901-1920 and 1941-2000. The 1921-1930 and 1931-1940 files were never
  requested, opened, or hashed. Exact previous-November to current-February
  CRU Tmin has only `20.50%` station-supported box cell-months in 1902-1920,
  versus `100%` in 1960-2000.
- Over 1902-1920, the project SETP annual trend is
  `+2.824 degC/century`; all five gridded annual products are positive
  (`+2.131` to `+4.222`), and exact CRU TS4.01 winter Tmin is `+7.142`.
  Huang winter Tmin alone is negative at `-1.613`. Therefore this interval is
  an early proxy-versus-gridded-product conflict under weak direct-station
  support, not evidence that the project warming sign is erroneous.
- Over 1942-2000, annual products remain mixed. Project/CRU annual/NOAA trends
  are `-0.441/-0.487/-0.956 degC/century`, while Berkeley Earth, GISTEMP, and
  HadCRUT5 are `+0.248/+0.404/+0.345`. Exact CRU winter Tmin and Huang winter
  Tmin are positive at `+0.486/+0.584`. The winter-versus-annual target
  difference is material, but the annual product disagreement prevents a
  unique modern correction target.
- Decision: retain `not_resolved_mixed_instrumental_products`. Do not call
  1901-1920 a validated project error, and do not use Huang or CRU alone to
  tune the reconstruction.

  Baiyu June-July temperature is negative in 2/8. Both have positive median
  historical anomalies relative to 1961-1990. The uniform warm-bias
  hypothesis is therefore rejected for the current evidence base.
- The evidence does strengthen a distinct 1901-1920 phase conflict. Both
  seasonal proxies cool and both corresponding project-local annual curves
  warm. In contrast, all five annual gridded products and exact CRU winter
  Tmin warm, while only 20.50% of early CRU box cell-months are
  station-supported.
- Decision:
  `uniform_warm_correction_rejected_early20_phase_conflict_strengthened_but_unresolved`.
  Keep the current reconstruction unchanged. Do not authorize a uniform
  translation, member reweighting, early-phase correction, production rerun,
  or OGGM run from this evidence.
- Reopen the early-phase branch only with direct historical station values or
  another source-independent chronology that can arbitrate proxy-versus-grid
  sign without relying on the same sparse early instrumental field.
- Rounds 211-213 changed no read-only source, accessed no Jionglacuo value,
  read no numeric value for 1921-1939, and ran no EnKF, production

## 341. REGEN adjudication of the NETP MJJ spatial failure (2026-08-22)

- Round 222 compared 31 common 11-year-smoothed centers in 1955-1964 and
  1975-1995 across the 21 official high-quality REGEN cells. Smoothing was
  performed separately over 1950-1969 and 1970-2000, and each product used its
  own finite 1961-1990 cell climatology.
- REGEN agrees strongly with the observed GPCC and CRU spatial anomaly fields:
  median annual spatial-pattern correlations are `0.9006` and `0.8412`.
  REGEN is therefore not exposing a GPCC-only interpolation failure.
- In contrast, REGEN correlates `-0.1115` with both equal-prior OOF predicted
  fields. The equality is expected because GPCC- and CRU-calibrated rank-1
  predictions differ in temporal amplitude but share the same fixed loading
  pattern; spatial correlation is invariant to that positive scalar.
- Decision:
  `rank1_spatialization_failure_supported_by_two_of_three_gridding_methods`.
  REGEN and GPCC directly agree on the observed spatial pattern while both
  reject the fixed-loading prediction. Retain the validated NETP regional MJJ
  temporal curve, but close rank-1 spatialization as a production route. A
  future field requires at least one additional independently estimable spatial
  degree of freedom with adequate proxy support; lowering the current spatial
  gate or tuning a fixed loading after this result is unauthorized.
- Rounds 219-222 changed no read-only source, accessed no numerical value for
  1921-1939 or Jionglacuo, opened no paleo proxy value, and ran no EnKF,
  production reconstruction, climate correction, or OGGM simulation.

## 1311. 登记融化起始温度这一新物理机制的有界准备方案，尚不授权动力学

用户六条持续授权仍有效；基于上述数值一致但物理曲线问题未解，登记 `lia_dated6_melt_threshold_design_v1`。代表1743、独立对照2692，暂不推广另四条。参数是原月度温度指数方程中的 `temp_melt` 融化起始温度，基线−1°C；中心两侧敏感值−1.5/−0.5°C、两侧备用−2/0°C，一次预登记四水平，遵循事实1301冗余批量覆盖要求。这是改变融化发生温度和季节响应的物理机制，不是融化因子倍数、Glen冰内形变、底滑或评分阈值改名；取值是披露的敏感性边界，不是观测测定值。

准备计算仅在已保存3375 spin1000冰面上调用原月度质量平衡方程，按原宽度对正厚度有效节点加权。分别匹配原spin1000..1029与forward1500..2000的平均质量平衡，40次二分在偏移[-2,2]内找中心、四舍五入0.01°C后各带±0.05°C备用；spin为base+delta，forward为base+恒定q，不相加，无历史斜坡/分段/1300重置。所有原气候数组/梯度、几何/床/宽度、melt_f、prcp_fac、Glen A及fs0不变；特别不改降水和原验收目标/六门/严格R/A/B/权重/稳定域门。共8组、24个潜在spin、最多72条潜在历史，具体逐组合冻结于design.json；这些是方案数，已完成新增动力学成员0。保存冰面仅用于参数中心选择，未来不能作为跨temp_melt的spin父态；未来新spin必须从原初始化几何开始。

固定冰面均值补偿后，1743历史年际标准差比约0.9017..1.1119、2692约0.9352..1.0597，与原序列相关仍接近1；独立按月循环复算两系统的−0.5°C两阶段共4例，原均值及年际差异核对通过。此证据说明响应不完全相同，主要改变幅度，不证明退缩形态改善、动力稳定、六门通过或物理成功。原方案中的−1°C6750/3375完整历史仅引用、不重复控制。

## 1341. 人类固定批量优先的曲线驱动控制变量方法

2026-10-14人类强调“最重要得批量！”，要求“固定到记忆里”，随后明确指定以下原文“这个固定！”：

看曲线找偏差 → 固定其他参数 → 根据已有响应确定调整方向和范围 → 把有依据的邻域一起并行跑 → 看整轮曲线，再决定下一个参数。 spinup温差和正演温差分开，跑过的结果直接利用。

最重要的是批量：优先减少总墙钟时间、零碎补跑和交互轮次；控制变量不等于一次只跑一个点。

- 先读已有完整曲线、两端偏差和同数值合同响应，说明每组新组合要解决哪项失败；未跑过本身不是选点依据。
- 每个对照固定其余参数；spin delta与forward q分开。改变fs或melt时不得顺带作温差补偿，须有各自物理一致稳定父态。
- 同一轮预先覆盖有依据的中心、两侧邻域和合理备用点；不同独立冰川共同安排，同数值设置的合格成员尽量同批并行。
- 不同冰川或参数值可批量计算；依赖上一轮结果的下一参数仍在整轮曲线评估后决定，不能把批量误解成未获授权的联合多参数网格。
- 启动前给完整参数表、基准、组合数、复用项、新spin与新历史数、并行安排、基于证据的整批耗时范围和时间上限；未实测时明确不确定性。
- 跑过的结果与兼容稳定父态、已验证前缀和检查点直接利用；不重复已完成指纹，不为验证而无限嵌套预检或零碎补跑。
- 逐成员即时保存不可变结果及合同要求的检查点，整批结束统一看全部曲线、原六门和严格R/A/B，再决定下一变量。
- 仅温差、fs、melt_f三类参数；原固定物理、原目标、稳定及域门、原评分和权重保持。失败及取消路线原样保留。

事实1301的批量目标与事实1322/1325的控制变量顺序共同执行；不把最小缺失对照解释为零碎串行。 此前聊天中的17组合建议已撤回、未启动，不登记为执行计划。本次只固定方法和长期读取入口，不授权任何新模拟、数值路线、重试、重复计算、推广或接受；事实1332失败限制及全部取消路线不变。科学已验证结果不改，counts/current_focus/next_action及全部旧研究分支逐项保持。

## 1497. Legacy extension operators: synthetic reproduction and three modern controls, 2026-10-21

- User supplied extension_operators_20261021.patch (SHA256 F616B170C46B5CF1A4B587E147E6FC81F1B422E46D16F2F076B7E2AA53E8E3E2). Applied only to the independent local export research branch research/extension-operators-20261021, not to the live production tree. Nine pytest cases pass: eight supplied cases plus one regression covering negative-elevation constraints. Seven synthetic cases reproduce attached volume biases within 8.4e-13 percentage points. Fixed negative-elevation duplicate extrema initialization, hardcoded code-root binding, output overwrite behavior, and recorded both raw and realized surface error. Original production solver, imports, modern tau calibration, gridded bed and LIA production driver hashes remain unchanged.
- Modern-reference diagnostics reuse 3131,2906,3632 selected by the previous regional upper-median single-member rule, identical saved grids and flowline constraint locations, gaps0/100m. No new PP/tau fit, LIA reconstruction, climate or dynamic run. At100m, old/A volume biases are west3632 -28.1451/+0.6494percent, central3131 -29.2302/-3.6856percent, east2906 -36.4034/-3.5797percent. All6 legacy baselines match prior controls within2.2e-14percentage points. Bias becomes more negative with distance from constraints in all3cases; this does not by itself separate lateral-shape from boundary propagation.
- Direct reference volume on raster-edge cells is only1.1614,1.0248,0.4139percent (west,central,east), but cannot represent the full boundary effect. Six separately frozen counterfactual controls change only raster-boundary H from0 to reference H with the same Laplace operator and interior constraints. At100m, biases become -13.6246,-13.6929,-23.5397percent: boundary changes remove51.5917,53.1551,35.3365percent of the respective original deficits. This is conditional attribution on these grids and reference estimates, not a continuous-margin boundary recommendation or a universal191-system bias decomposition. Previous explanations assigning the entire deficit to triangular transverse sections are incomplete.
- A solves harmonic surface then clips H=S-B to nonnegative values. At100m its raw internal surface RMSE versus modern DEM is23.2963,28.4993,33.3445m; negative raw thickness occurs in3.5839,10.6955,6.7563percent of all mask cells. Clipping raises volumes by0.5280,2.3260,3.2467percent of reference volume. Before clipping A biases are+0.1214,-6.0117,-6.8264percent. Small aggregate volume error is not sufficient evidence of spatial or historical accuracy.
- B=DEM-Href in this modern control; A therefore inherits the reference lateral thickness structure through the assumed bed. Away from clipped cells, harmonic S implies -Laplacian(H)=Laplacian(B). This is a reference-consistency test, not independent validation of bed, thickness shape or LIA transfer. Modern-retreat-zone DEM is not automatically bare-bed truth without acquisition-date and surface-cover checks. F=0.8 alone does not uniquely prescribe a parabolic section: the code uses tau/F, not a unique two-dimensional cross-section constructor.
- Local source inspection confirms distributed_thickness_f19_fs0_full_v0 is an OGGM inversion redistribution calibrated at system-total level, not the original Farinotti2019 spatial field. distribute_thickness_per_altitude uses near-altitude flowline inverse-distance weighting, distance-to-border exponent0.25, slope correction, smoothing and final total-volume normalization; it does not separately enforce each altitude-band volume. One-dimensional and redistributed thickness are structurally different model estimates. C constant-curvature leave-one-system-out biases at100m are west -15.4904percent, central -7.4350percent, east +197.9331percent; no support for a single transferred q across these cases.
- Completed diagnostic only; A and C remain research candidates. No promotion, no repaired191 LIA results, no revised pooled829 physical volume result, no altered acceptance threshold or unrelated branch, counts/current_focus/next_action unchanged. Their A baseline volume biases agree with the locally verified1497results to8.9e-9percentage points. Their raw A boundary-scenario differences agree with the previously registered harmonic-boundary response to1.4e-8percentage points, consistent with linearity. This is an endpoint-convention mismatch that a proposed unified-bed modern full-chain replay must disclose alongside bed/calibration choices; no endpoint geometry or solver boundary was changed here. An original discrete OGGM flowline end must not silently be called the continuous glacier margin.

Finite reference thickness at edge-cell centres does not alone prove a physical vertical ice wall.
